Gantu then sent the pod to [[Dr. Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]], who activated it and got smothered in 054's chocolate. Reuben raved about Gantu's karma, only to get punched by the ex-captain. 054, named Fudgy, reappeared in "[[Snafu (episode)|Snafu]]", and was freed along with Gantu's other captive experiments by [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]], [[Stitch]], and several other experiments in a rescue mission. ===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''=== The first 624 experiments, including Fudgy, were rounded up by [[Leroy]] and taken to a stadium to be destroyed. However, [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]], [[Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben]], and [[Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed. It is unknown whether or not Fudgy participated in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]]. The Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle, but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben, and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe. ===''[[Stitch!]]''=== Fudgy made an appearance in the ''Stitch!'' anime where [[Dr. Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]] used him to invade a chocolate factory. The plan was to turn [[Stitch]] into chocolate and have Fudgy eat him, thus imprisoning Stitch in his chocolaty stomach-prison. However, the factory starts going haywire and covers [[Yuna Kamihara|Yuna]] and company in chocolate. In a feeding frenzy, Fudgy swallows them all. Luckily, Hämsterviel didn't alter Fudgy's fail-safe. Stitch covers himself in chocolate to force Fudgy to eat him so he can infiltrate Fudgy's stomach-prison. Stitch and friends are able to stop Fudgy by expressing their love for each other, causing Fudgy to melt apart and free everyone. After Fudgy is neutralized, he reverts to his smaller size before being captured by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] and [[Pleakley]]. Fudgy was presumably reverted back to normal, then dehydrated back into an experiment pod and stored in Jumba's vault. Eventually, Jumba grabbed his pod to help Stitch in his fight against [[Dark End]], but Fudgy wasn't one of the experiments that was activated. ==Gallery== {{Gallerylink|Fudgy/Gallery}} ==Trivia== *Fudgy is Experiment 054. However, in [[Houdini (episode)|his debut]], his [[Experiment Pods|pod]] is labeled 119 and also mistaken for Experiment 611 ([[Experiments#Battlefield and doomsday experiments with galactic implications|El Fin]]), most likely due to Jumba's untidy [[Jumba's Computer|database]]. **An ironic coincidence in Fudgy being confused for another experiment because his pod was inverted is that Experiment 119's code name is [[Experiments#1-Series: Civic disturbances|Inverto]]. **Even though we saw Fudgy in pod form, he was activated off-screen. **Additionally, even though Fudgy technically debuted in the first season, we do not see him fully until "[[Snafu (episode)|Snafu]]" near the end of the second season. *Fudgy and [[Experiments#0-Series: Jumba's test batch, including many household helpers|Coco]] are the only known experiments with primary functions directly involving chocolate, and both of their names relate to chocolate as well. Interestingly, their numbers are close together. *Fudgy, [[Phantasmo]], [[Remmy]], [[Tickle-Tummy]], and [[Witch (Lilo & Stitch)|Witch]] are the only known experiments to have arms but no legs. *Fudgy's pod color is blue in [[Lilo & Stitch: The Series|the original series]]. In the ''[[Stitch!]]'' anime, it is red. *Fudgy was possibly mentioned in "[[Skip (episode)|Skip]]" by [[Captain Gantu|Gantu]] as a brown one, when he was telling [[Dr. Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]] which experiments he caught. *Fudgy is one of the few experiments to not have his one true place revealed. *He is also one of the few experiments to not appear in the group photo at the end of ''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''. *In the anime, Fudgy is seen with the ability to grow larger from eating chocolate, similar to [[Tank (Lilo & Stitch)|Tank]]'s ability to grow larger from eating metal and [[Ploot]]'s ability to grow larger from eating garbage. ==External links== *{{L&S|Fudgy (054)}} {{Lilo & Stitch}} [[Category:Lilo & Stitch Experiments]] [[Category:Lilo & Stitch characters]] [[Category:Males]] [[Category:Aliens]] [[Category:Creatures]] [[Category:Disney characters]] [[Category:Animated characters]] [[Category:Monsters]] [[Category:Neutral characters]] [[Category:Silent characters]] [[Category:Stitch! characters]]

[[Experiments]] ("cousins")}} '''Frenchfry''', also known as '''Experiment 062''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. He is designed to be Jumba's personal chef and prepare delectable, irresistible meals, but had a flaw in his programming that caused him to remove all nutrition from his cooking, while those who ate his food would bloat up rapidly, after which he would eat them. If the victim managed to escape, the bloating would wear off after 24 hours. His one true place is running a healthy French fry hut and making delicious low-fat food, but his actions have promoted him to a restaurant chef. ==Background== ===Personality=== Frenchfry initially enjoyed causing chaos and mischief through his gourmet cooking. Ironically, however, this was not his intentional programming when he was instead to simply be [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]]'s personal chef. He enjoys making food and being complimented for it, appearing friendly and helpful. However, he is actually sneaky and conniving, as he plans on eating the victims he feeds by constantly bombarding them with food, even when they try to restrain themselves, knowing they can't resist his food. After being captured by [[Nani Pelekai|Nani]] and enjoying her oatmeal, he decides to eat healthily and no longer has the desire to eat individuals, but still retains his love of cooking. He is also seen to be quite talkative, as he tends to speak [[France|French]] with a heavy accent. ===Physical appearance=== Frenchfry is a small, gray, mustached experiment with four arms with three fingers on each hand, black eyes, a red round nose, short ears, and a spatula for a tail. He has a white bulbous forehead resembling a chef's hat and white markings around his eyes, stomach, tail, and head. ===Powers and abilities=== Frenchfry is a talented chef who can move at lightning speeds and whip up massive meals in seconds, and anything he makes is irresistible and delectable. His foods take up no apparent space in the eater's stomach, regardless of how much, and he originally removed all nutrition from his meals, therefore causing consumers to bloat vastly in size, whom he originally ate once properly fattened. According to Jumba when Frenchfry was his personal chef, the consumer can bloat up to a size of a spaceship. Frenchfry can also morph into a miniature tornado and is skilled with any and every cooking utensil, which he can turn into a weapon. ==Appearances== ===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''=== Experiment 062 was the 62nd genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Dr. Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to be Jumba's personal chef, but instead made unhealthy food that quickly made individuals fat and overweight, then ate the fattened victims. Presumably, when the food fattened Jumba up to a massive enough size, 062 tried to eat him, but Jumba was able to deactivate him in time. 062 and the other first 624 experiments were later smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch|Experiment 626]]. All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of Kauai. At an unknown point after this, Experiment 062's pod was found by Jumba and kept hidden away. After [[Nani Pelekai|Nani]] began restricting [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]] and [[Stitch]]'s diet to healthy food, she told [[Pleakley]] to feed them the nutritious meals she left in the freezer before heading to work. However, Lilo, Stitch, and Pleakley defied Nani and found 062's pod in a drawer while searching [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]]'s room for a stash of junk food. When Lilo and Stitch discovered what 062 was created to do, they activated the latter and asked him to make them junk food. 062, named Frenchfry by Lilo, complied but secretly designed the food to fatten Lilo, Stitch, and Pleakley up while still being irresistibly delicious, which would culminate in him eating them. After a while, Lilo grew suspicious of their abnormal bloating, so she and Stitch tried to learn more about Frenchfry on [[Jumba's Computer|Jumba's computer]], although none of its data was helpful to them whatsoever. Frenchfry then distracted the two with a tray of doughnuts, fattening them up even more. [[Captain Gantu|Gantu]] managed to [[Prison Capsule|capture]] Frenchfry at one point by imitating a "trog call" to lure him out of the [[Lilo's House|Pelekai residence]]. However, after taking a beating from a bloated Lilo and Stitch, Gantu proclaimed that it was his birthday (although he denied this earlier when [[Reuben|Experiment 625]] mentioned it). Frenchfry then made Gantu a cake that he devoured, which fattened him up and caused him to flee in shock. While Frenchfry continued to make Lilo, Stitch, and Pleakley more bloating food, Lilo called Jumba at a public event to find out more about the chef experiment. However, Jumba just barely finished revealing Frenchfry's true intentions when the latter cut the phone line with a pair of pliers. Lilo and Stitch finally became so bloated from all the unhealthy food that Frenchfry restrained them and attempted to eat them. Before he could do so, Nani, who had heard from Jumba while at work, promptly arrived home and battled and defeated Frenchfry, eventually trapping him under Lilo's wading pool. The next morning, Lilo and Stitch (back to their trim selves) discovered that Frenchfry had taken a liking to Nani's oatmeal, which Lilo and Stitch initially refused to eat until Nani cleverly enticed them. Thus, they agreed to feed him oatmeal, and in return, he vowed to make healthy meals and not try to eat people. Frenchfry shortly after found his one true place running a healthy French fry hut, where he made delicious low-fat food. In "[[Remmy (episode)|Remmy]]", Frenchfry was one of the experiments in Lilo's dream. ===''[[The Origin of Stitch]]''=== Frenchfry was one of the experiments that were gliding on the screen, but he is 558 instead of 062. ===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''=== Frenchfry was seen early in the movie giving [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]] some low-fat French fries as she was making her rounds with [[Scrump]] to make sure all the experiments were happy in the one true place they belonged. '''Welko''', also known as '''Experiment 074''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. She is designed to blow temporary indestructible bubbles. She appears in the ''[[Stitch!]]'' anime.

==Background==
Experiment 074 was the 74th genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Dr. Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel's]] funding. She was designed to produce temporary indestructible bubbles. 074 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch|Experiment 626]].

All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of Kauai.

===Physical appearance===
Welko is a pink, balloon-shaped doglike experiment with dark blue eyes, orbs on either side of her head, big red lips, and a red heart-like tail. Her hind legs appear to be vestigial nubs, and she seems to be constantly levitating. It is unknown if she is capable of terrestrial locomotion.

===Powers and abilities===
Welko can blow indestructible bubbles from her mouth that last only temporarily. Her bubbles are able to somewhat stick together, and thus can be formed into a cloud. Her body contains a form of helium or another light air, and this causes her to float.

Through some means, she can inflate indestructible balloons that last around 30 minutes. Such means are probably accomplished through her tail or the pink orbs on her head, which is in the same shape as some of her balloons.

==Appearances==
===''[[Stitch!]]''===
Welko first appeared when [[Captain Gantu|Gantu]] gained possession of her through unknown means and used her in [[Dr. Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s sinister plot to get rid of [[Stitch]].

Stitch gets kidnapped and tied to one of Welko's balloons during the foretasted typhoon, where he would drown when the balloon popped and have no chance of survival, as he would be restrained from movement. The bubble cloud suddenly pops beneath Hämsterviel, and he plummets to the ground. Later, Gantu sets a trap for Stitch with Welko accompanying him, but [[Yuna Kamihara|Yuna]] falls into it instead when she is looking for Stitch.

The plan changes and it is decided that Yuna would be bait for Stitch, so they suspend her in a hot air balloon made of dozens of Welko's balloons. Nobody notices Yuna until five minutes before the balloons pop. When the clock reaches zero, her makeshift gondola hits the water, and Stitch dives in to save her, almost making it before sinking. [[Tigerlily]] then saves them both.

The fate of Welko after this is unknown.

==Trivia==
*Her unique design is a reference to animal-shaped {{WikipediaLink|Balloon modeling|balloon art}}.
*Welko is one of the rare experiments to not have black eyes like most experiments, having dark blue eyes instead. Interestingly, she shares this trait with [[Bonnie (Lilo & Stitch)|Bonnie]], [[Tickle-Tummy]], and [[Witch (Lilo & Stitch)|Witch]], three other female experiments.
*Welko, [[Zap]], [[Remmy]], [[Cloudy]], and [[Shrink]] are the only known experiments that are always seen levitating.
**[[Phantasmo]] and Witch primarily levitate but often possess objects or living beings to move by other means. Tickle-Tummy is also able to levitate, but has been seen bouncing as well.

Time warper |home = [[Hawaii]] |likes = Skipping ten years |dislikes = Being captured |powers = Time-jumping |status = Active |creator = [[Jumba Jookiba]] |family = [[Experiments]] ("cousins")}} '''Skip''', also known as '''Experiment 089''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. He is designed to skip time by ten minutes, but had a flaw in his programming that made him skip ahead ten years instead. When used by someone, the individual and whoever is beside him will travel forward in time by one decade. Luckily, he has a reset button that will bring the time travelers back to the original time they started in. ==Background== ===Personality=== Rather than being a troublesome experiment, Skip is rather wobbly and clumsy and enjoys exploring his surroundings. He is also surprisingly happy-go-lucky and easygoing, often smiling and not caring about being confined. Unlike most of his cousins, he doesn't cause trouble on purpose, but tends to cause unforeseen consequences when someone activates his powers. He seems slightly dazed at times, not paying attention to what others are saying and not being observant of his surroundings. ===Physical appearance=== Skip is a plump, purple hourglass-shaped experiment with a large head, on top of which is two green dots forming the button to activate his power. He has small white eyes with black pupils, a red nose, and a wide mouth. ===Powers and abilities=== Skip can transport himself and anyone near him ten years into the future each time his button is pressed; they will also age ten years with each "skip". However, the people who travel with him will be sent into the future in a time period in which they were absent during the ten years skipped, causing causality paradoxes. Luckily, Skip also has a reverse setting that sends him and his users back to the present day by pressing his button while he's upside down and the entire future they had traveled into will be permanently erased from the timeline. ==Appearances== ===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''=== Experiment 089 was the 89th genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Dr. Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was originally designed to skip time ahead by ten minutes (because Jumba was too impatient to wait for his microwave to reheat his leftovers), but there was an error in his programming; when the button on 089's head was pressed, he instead skipped ahead ten years. 089 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch|Experiment 626]]. All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of Kauai. At an unknown point, Experiment 089 was activated and then taken in by the [[Aloha Animal Rescue|dog shelter]]. When [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]] went to visit the pound and asked the [[Susan Hegarty|dog pound lady]] if there had been any new "dogs" brought here lately, the latter presented 089 to Lilo. She then adopted 089 from the dog shelter and took him back to [[Lilo's House|her house]]. After [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] explained 089's powers to Lilo, she named him Skip. Having grown tired of childhood restrictions, Lilo used the experiment to skip her and [[Stitch]] ahead ten years and become a teenager. Unfortunately, life for Lilo and Stitch in this future quickly proved to be inconvenient when they went into [[Kokaua Town|town]] using [[Nani Pelekai|Nani]]'s [[X-Buggy|dune buggy]], as they were relentlessly given tickets by local police and discovered [[Dr. Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]] working undercover as a parking officer. Believing she needed to be even older to fulfill her desires, Lilo used Skip (despite Stitch's reluctance) to flash forward another ten years and become a full-fledged adult. However, Lilo, Stitch, and Skip were sent into an alternate future where, in their absence, Hämsterviel had become supreme ruler of the world, with Kokaua Town renamed "Hämsterviel Ville" as its capital, and almost every experiment in his custody (with Stitch and Skip still wanted). The trio were puzzled and horrified by this setback, but before they could investigate further, Stitch and Skip were captured by future police backed up by [[Clink]] and taken to [[Captain Gantu|Gantu]], despite Lilo's best efforts to protect them. She managed to escape while promising to come back for them, with the police letting her go, as their boss only cared about the experiments. When Lilo returned home, a tattered Jumba explained that while she and Stitch were gone for twenty years, their house was repossessed to cover unpaid parking tickets regarding Nani's dune buggy that Lilo had borrowed as a teen ten years from the current day. Jumba then added that he had been hiding in the attic ever since Hämsterviel had taken power and captured all the other experiments because Lilo and Stitch were not here at the time to do it themselves. Unfortunately, Nani had to work for Hämsterviel to pay off any debts. Later on, Stitch and Skip were rescued by Lilo, Jumba, and [[Pleakley]] (who became an intergalactic fashion celebrity with top ten TV shows in the intergalactic fashion channel) while Gantu was distracted. Lilo then used Skip's reverse function, which Jumba revealed, to return her and Stitch to the present. He can talk extremely fast in a high-pitched, squeaky voice, hence his name. ==Appearances== ===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''=== Experiment 110 was the 110th genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Dr. Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. {{Dablink|the [[Stitch!]] experiment|cartoon characters in general|[[Toon]]}} {{Infobox character |image = Experiment 112 "Toons" Stitch! profile.webp |shows = ''[[Stitch!]]'' |alias = Experiment 112 |likes = Making pictures come to life |powers = Turns everyone into cartoons (original)

Converts two-dimensional images into three-dimensional physical beings and objects (reprogrammed) |status = Dehydrated |creator = [[Jumba Jookiba]] |family = [[Experiments]] ("cousins")}} '''Toons''', also known as '''Experiment 112''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. He is designed to turn anyone into a cartoon. When transmuted by [[Dr. Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]], he can transform into the subject of any drawing inserted into his mouth. When reprogrammed, he can bring 2D images to life in 3D. He appears in the ''[[Stitch!]]'' anime. ==Background== Experiment 112 was the 112th genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Dr. Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to either turn everyone into cartoons, turn into the subject of any pictures, or bring 2D pictures to life. 112 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch|Experiment 626]]. All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of Kauai. ===Physical appearance=== Toons is a yellow platypus/{{WikipediaLink|axolotl}}-like experiment with an orange mane and a rectangular vacuum-like mouth. ===Powers and abilities=== Toons' function and abilities changed over the course of two reprograms, so he has three functions at different stages: #'''Original:''' He can turn anyone into a cartoon. #'''Transmuted:''' He can transform into the subject of any drawing inserted into his mouth. #'''Reprogrammed:''' He can bring 2D images to life by consuming the 2D subject and spitting it back out, making it appear 3D. Spinning Toons' collar counterclockwise reverts his creations back to their original state. ==Appearances== ===''[[Stitch!]]''=== Toons appeared in two episodes of the third season of the ''Stitch!'' anime. His debut was in "Spooky Toons" as one of two transmutated experiments under [[Dr. Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s control to capture [[Stitch]] (the other being [[Spooky]]). When [[Captain Gantu|Gantu]] and [[Reuben]] arrived at the island [[Yuna Kamihara|Yuna]]'s class was staying on, her drawing of a false island legend (which had blown away in the breeze) smacked into Gantu's face. He thought it was scary and decided to give it to Toons to help in Stitch's capture. Toons then turned into the drawing. Later, after Yuna, Stitch, [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Dolores (Stitch!)|Dolores]], and [[BooGoo]] managed to convince [[Jessica (Stitch!)|Jessica]] that the legend was real, she let out a sneeze, which (according to Dolores) caused the monster to appear. Coincidentally, after she sneezed, Toons (transformed into the monster) showed up. Per Gantu's orders, he tried to capture Stitch. While they fought, Jumba saw the H-mark on his forehead and figured out who he really was. He then drew a small picture of a butterfly and told Stitch to feed it into the monster's mouth. Stitch complied and due to Toons' programming, he turned from a giant monster into a small butterfly and was easily captured. After his capture, a machine built by Jumba reversed Hämsterviel's reprogramming and turned Toons back to normal. He was then dehydrated and stored in Jumba's secret vault until he was needed again. In his second episode "Shogun", Yuna had to do a report on ancient Japanese warriors, including what they ate. But when she looked in the history book Pleakley showed her, she couldn't make out what the shogun in the picture was eating. Pleakley mentioned that Toons could help as he was designed to bring pictures to life, but he was locked in Jumba's vault. Fortunately, Yuna knew the codes to open it. She then took Toons' pod and dropped it in a glass of water, reactivating him. She fed the whole book into his mouth, and he animated not only was the shogun was eating, but Shogun himself! Unfortunately, Jumba was away and since no one else knew how to reverse Toons' work, they were stuck with him. Later, Jumba returned and would help Shogun go back to where he came from. Before he left, [[Tigerlily Sakai|Tigerlily]] gave him a big plate of spaghetti (which he had developed a fondness for) as a parting gift. Jumba then grabbed Toons' mane and spun it like a disk counterclockwise. Shogun was sucked back into Toons and turned back into the history book, much to Tigerlily's shock and dismay. The next morning, Stitch shows Yuna and Tigerlily the picture again and in it, Shogun is eating Tigerlily's spaghetti! Toons was dehydrated again and was put back in Jumba's vault. Eventually, Jumba grabbed his pod to help Stitch in his fight against [[Dark End]], but Toons wasn't one of the experiments that was activated. ==Trivia== *Toons is the only experiment introduced in ''[[Stitch!]]'' that appeared activated in more than one episode, having appeared activated in two different episodes. *Although Toons' original function was to turn everyone into cartoons, after being reprogrammed, his new function was to bring images to life. **His original function and function after reprogramming are opposite in action. **Also, reversing his reprogrammed function (by spinning his collar) is similar to his original one. *Toons' [[Experiment Pods|pod]] color is green. *Toons and [[Bragg]] are the only ''Stitch!'' experiments whose functions were changed after their transmutation. *Although Toons makes sounds in the English dub, his English voice actor was never credited. ==Gallery== Stitch! - Shogun - Toons' pod dropped in water.png|Toons' experiment pod Toonh1.png Toonsh2.png|試作品112号トゥーンズ translates to Prototype No. 122 Toons screenCapture 25.03.13 20-54-09.jpg screenCapture 25.03.13 20-55-06.jpg screenCapture 25.03.13 20-55-24.jpg screenCapture 25.03.13 20-56-04.jpg screenCapture 25.03.13 20-56-46.jpg screenCapture 25.03.13 20-57-13.jpg screenCapture 25.03.13 20-57-39.jpg screenCapture 25.03.13 20-58-44.jpg screenCapture 25.03.13 20-59-08.jpg screenCapture 25.03.13 20-59-45.jpg screenCapture 14.05.13 19-03-00.jpg ==External links== *{{L&S|Toons (112)}} {{Lilo & Stitch}} [[Category:Males]] [[Category:Stitch! characters]] [[Category:Lilo & Stitch Experiments]] [[Category:Aliens]] [[Category:Creatures]] [[Category:Disney characters]] [[Category:Animated characters]] [[Category:Silent characters]] [[Category:Anime characters]]

Bad/good luck inducer |home = [[Hawaii]] |likes = Bringing good luck |dislikes = Bringing bad luck |powers = Luck manipulation |status = Active |creator = [[Jumba Jookiba]] |family = [[Experiments]] ("cousins")}} '''Shoe''', also known as '''Experiment 113''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. He is designed to generate negative events; however, adjusting his cranial horseshoe controls the type of event (luck) generated. In a downward position, he causes bad luck; in an upright position, he causes good luck. His one true place is at the mini-golf course, making miniature golfers score holes-in-one. ==Background== ===Personality=== Shoe appears to be mute, but also friendly and sociable as shown when he tried to make friends with [[Stitch]]. Unlike most experiments, Shoe doesn't mean to cause chaos intentionally; it is merely the way he was programmed. He is also shown to be very sensitive about his bad luck powers, as seen when he overheard [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]] say that he cannot seem to change his bad luck and is apparently useless. He felt abandoned and hurt after hearing this and even ran away. However, when Lilo learned that Shoe could generate good luck, she apologized to him after finding him, and he seemed to forgive Lilo when he hugged her. ===Physical appearance=== Shoe is a green, lanky experiment with a horseshoe-shaped head, a pointed face with black eyes, small dark purple round nose, and two long curved horns with white tips that are shaped like a horseshoe. The horns can be flipped upward or downward. ===Powers and abilities=== Shoe is a luck-manipulating experiment. When his cranial horseshoe, or the "horns" on his head, are facing down, bad luck occurs; when the horseshoe is turned up, good luck occurs. The events can be predicted to happen whenever the tips of his horns glow, and also a faint bleep is heard. Shoe cannot control the luck his powers provide to himself or others, however, and is dependent on the horns' position. ==Appearances== ===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''=== Experiment 113 was the 113th genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Dr. Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to generate bad luck, but could also cause good luck. 113 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch|Experiment 626]]. All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of Kauai, with 113's pod landing on a miniature golf course. 113's pod was used as a golf ball, where a miniature golfer whacked it. The pod landed in the moat obstacle, activating 113, who then went around the island causing bad luck. [[Captain Gantu|Gantu]] had been informed about 113, but [[Dr. Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]] refused to have a bad luck experiment. Gantu then had a squabble with [[Reuben|Experiment 625]], who tried to tell the former about 113's good luck ability. When Reuben later managed to reveal this to Gantu (and deftly tape-recorded his earlier protests), the latter then decided to track down and capture 113. Meanwhile, 113, traveled to the [[Lilo's House|Pelekai residence]], where his bad luck caused [[Nani Pelekai|Nani]]'s jeep to break down, thus forcing her to walk to work. He was later caught raiding the kitchen by [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]], [[Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], and [[Pleakley]]. 113 kept generating bad luck for Lilo's ''[[Pelekai ʻohana|ʻohana]]'', despite their best efforts to change his bad luck effects and hide him someplace where the bad luck he created could not affect them. When Lilo reluctantly admitted that 113, named Shoe, was a jinx and unable to bring good luck, the latter, unfortunately, overheard her and promptly left, feeling hurt and abandoned. After Jumba revealed that Shoe could generate good luck, Lilo and Stitch set out to find him. The two discovered Shoe sitting alone on a cliff, but before they could act, Gantu overtook Stitch and scooped Shoe in a [[Prison Capsule|container]]. Despite being captured, Shoe's bad luck allowed him to evade both Gantu and Stitch. After a series of mishaps, Gantu managed to reclaim Shoe and turned the latter's horns upward, causing him to generate good luck for Gantu. Shoe was then left alone on [[Lahui Beach|the beach]] after his good luck caused Gantu to become rich, making the experiment feel just as useless as when he generated bad luck. Shoe was eventually found by Lilo, who apologized to the former for giving up on him. After generating good luck for Lilo's ''ʻohana'' and bad luck for Gantu, Shoe found his one true place at a mini-golf course (the same one where he was activated) using his "good luck setting" to allow golfers to score holes-in-one. In "[[Skip (episode)|Skip]]", Shoe was one of the wanted fugitives who had already been captured in an alternate future where Hämsterviel ruled Earth. ===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''=== The first 624 experiments, including Shoe, were rounded up by [[Leroy]] and taken to a stadium to be destroyed. However, [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]], [[Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben]], and [[Captain Gantu|Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed. Shoe participated in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]], but it is unknown what he did. The Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle, but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben, and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe. ==Gallery== {{Gallerylink}} ==Trivia== *Lilo stated that she didn't name 113 "Shoe" because of his horseshoe-like horn, but because she thinks he needs shoes, despite the fact that none of the experiments wear shoes. **According to [[Jess Winfield]] on his TV Tome thread, in real life, Shoe was actually partly named after a production associate, Jennifer "Shoe" Hsyu.{{cite web|url=http://lasfansite.atspace.me/stuff/history/tvtome/page04.html|title=L&S Says Mahalo|website={{WikipediaLink|TV.com|TV Tome}}|date=December 14, 2004|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20160305082355/http://lasfansite.atspace.me/stuff/history/tvtome/page04.html|archivedate=March 19, 2016|accessdate=May 27, 2018}} *According to Jumba, the moment he created Shoe, his [[Galaxy Defense Industries|laboratory]] exploded. *Altering the position of Shoe's U-shaped horn in order to reverse his powers is the same way to reverse the effects of [[Dorkifier]]. Also, the closeness of their numbers (113 and 122) and movable horn feature may suggest that Jumba had been inspired by the same DNA source when creating both experiments. This would be a similar concept to how Jumba reused some of Twang's DNA when creating [[Bragg]]. *Shoe's [[Experiment Pods|pod]] color is purple. *The [[Experiment Pod Container]] describes Shoe as: "Experiment 113. Primary function: Negative event generator." *His number is a likely reference to the number 13, which is considered unlucky by most Western cultures. *Shoe's holographic silhouette appeared in "[[Snooty (episode)|Snooty]]". **Shoe is shown to have two different graphic designs on [[Jumba's Computer|Jumba's computer]]. ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== *{{L&S|Shoe (113)}} {{Lilo & Stitch}} [[Category:Lilo & Stitch Experiments]] [[Category:Lilo & Stitch characters]] [[Category:Males]] [[Category:Creatures]] [[Category:Aliens]] [[Category:Disney characters]] [[Category:Animated characters]] [[Category:Silent characters]]
Snafu:
{{Infobox character |image = Profile - Snafu.png |voice = [[Frank Welker]] |films = ''[[Leroy & Stitch]]'' |shows = ''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]'' |alias = Experiment 120 |occupation = Jumba's 120th experiment
Plan thwarter |home = [[Hawaii]] |likes = Foiling enemy plans |dislikes = His plans backfiring, being captured |powers = Expert saboteur |status = Active |creator = [[Jumba Jookiba]] |family = [[Experiments]] ("cousins")}} '''Snafu''', also known as '''Experiment 120''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. He is designed to discombobulate enemy plans by any possible means; he will also thwart any attempt to capture him, and thus can only be caught by accident. ==Background== ===Personality=== Snafu is a mischievous, cunning, and conniving experiment. This is proven when he turned all of [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]] and [[Stitch]]'s plans to save the imprisoned experiments in [[Gantu's Ship|Gantu's ship]] against them, and even sabotaged [[Captain Gantu|Gantu]]'s plans to turn all the redeemed experiments from good to back to bad by swapping the tape of [[Angel (Lilo & Stitch)|Angel]]'s song with Gantu's karaoke tape. However, his desire to foil plans seems to come from his programming, and he is initially unable to distinguish friend and foe. Snafu seems to be somewhat sadistic, as he laughs every time he manages to foil a plan. Since he was programmed to sabotage enemy plans by any possible means, he is very resourceful, with even Jumba acknowledging that he can only be caught by accident. The only thing Snafu hates the most is having his own sabotage backfire on him. However, after Stitch revealed his love to Angel, Snafu became touched while shedding tears and changed his heart. ===Physical appearance=== Snafu is a small dark-green cephalopod-like experiment with a roughly reptilian face and white eyes. He has small limbs and a tail, black markings on his back, and six telescoping prehensile tentacles on his large dome head. ===Powers and abilities=== Snafu is a master at foiling any and all complex plans. He is also highly elusive due to his plan-foiling skills, and can only be captured or defeated by accident. He often uses his tentacles for mobility or gripping objects. His eyes can serve as magnifying lenses and has an incredible ability to tamper with machines. ==Appearances== ===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''=== Experiment 120 was the 120th genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Dr. Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to foil any and all enemy plans at whatever cost. 120 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch|Experiment 626]]. All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of Kauai. At an unknown point after this, Experiment 120's pod was found by Jumba and kept in a shoebox under his bed. [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]] discovered 120's pod in the shoebox under [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]]'s bed when she was searching around his room for any unactivated experiments to use in a rescue mission to free [[Stitch]]'s cousins on [[Gantu's Ship|Gantu's ship]]. However, Jumba took 120's pod from Lilo and revealed its design. Jumba warned Lilo not to use 120, as he was the worst experiment to activate when making complex rescue missions. Just then, [[Pleakley]] foolishly came in with a hose and sprayed water everywhere, which got 120's pod wet, activating the experiment. 120 ripped up the blueprints for Lilo and Stitch's rescue mission and then escaped through the pet flap. 120 remained near the [[Lilo's House|Pelekai residence]], where he cleverly spied on Lilo, Stitch, and the experiments' plans for the rescue mission and sabotaged their obstacle course, which put a damper on things. 120 later foiled [[Captain Gantu|Gantu]]'s plan to revert all of the rehabilitated experiments to evil by swapping the tape of [[Angel (Lilo & Stitch)|Angel]]'s song with Gantu's karaoke tape. When the tape was played by [[Reuben|Experiment 625]] driving a stolen ice cream truck, everyone in [[Kokaua Town|town]] became awestruck and laughed in amusement, thinking it was a prank, much to Gantu's embarrassment. When Lilo, Stitch, and the experiments launched a rescue mission on the ship, 120 tricked [[Sample]] into imitating the ship's alarm to alert Gantu. 120 then rewired the ship's prison, causing it to trap Lilo and the rescue team. However, 120, named Snafu, did not count on the prison trapping him as well. Though after hearing Stitch confess his love for Angel, Snafu cried because it really touched his heart, causing him to turn from bad to good. Fortunately, Snafu was freed by Angel and Stitch, who also freed Lilo and the other captive experiments in their [[Prison Capsule|containment orbs]]. Snafu then foiled Gantu before the latter could recapture the experiments and escaped the ship with Lilo, the rescue team, and the released experiments. ===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''=== The first 624 experiments, including Snafu, were rounded up by [[Leroy]] and taken to a stadium to be destroyed. However, [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]], [[Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben]], and [[Captain Gantu|Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed. It is unknown whether or not Snafu participated in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]]. The Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle, but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben, and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down, due to the original Leroy's fail-safe. ==Gallery== {{Gallerylink}} ==Trivia== *Snafu is named after the acronym {{WikipediaLink|SNAFU}} ('''S'''ituation '''N'''ormal: '''A'''ll '''F'''ouled '''U'''p). *According to Jumba, Snafu is a "havoc wreaker of all havoc wreakers." *Snafu's [[Experiment Pods|pod]] color is purple. *The [[Experiment Pod Container]] describes Snafu as: "Experiment 120. Primary function: Discombobulates enemy plans." *Snafu is one of the few experiments to not have his one true place revealed. *He is also one of the few experiments to not appear in the group photo at the end of ''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''. ==External links== *{{L&S|Snafu (120)}} {{Lilo & Stitch}} [[Category:Lilo & Stitch characters]] [[Category:Aliens]] [[Category:Males]] [[Category:Monsters]] [[Category:Spies]] [[Category:Creatures]] [[Category:Disney characters]] [[Category:Lilo & Stitch Experiments]] [[Category:Animated characters]] [[Category:Silent characters]] [[Category:Heroes]]

[[Experiments]] ("cousins")}} '''Carmen''', also known as '''Experiment 123''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. She is designed to make victims dance until they drop with her infectious Latin beats. ==Background== ===Physical appearance=== Carmen is a pink, blue-eyed, four-armed, [[Angel (Lilo & Stitch)|Angel]]-like experiment with a red nose and dark purple-tipped ears, wearing a headdress of fruit and holding a maraca in each of her four hands. Carmen has dark pink fur with splashes of light pink fur on her limbs. Her belly is also light pink. She is somewhat curvier than Angel, but her legs are the shortest of any other experiment with a similar build. She keeps all four of her long arms exposed at all times. Her eyes and tongue are a robin's-egg blue. Two short antennae extend just beneath her ears. Her most outstanding feature is the fruit salad she wears on her head, which includes bananas, grapes, oranges, cherries, and pineapples. She also carries four festive maracas at all times that help her carry out her primary function. ===Powers and abilities=== Carmen makes victims dance until they drop by firing pink balls of energy out of her maracas that pop when they take effect. She can also cancel the effect by clapping the maracas together. ==Appearances== ===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''=== Experiment 123 was the 123rd genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Dr. Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]] 's funding. She was designed to make victims dance until they drop. 123 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch|Experiment 626]]. All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of Kauai. At some point, 123 was activated, captured, tamed, and named Carmen. ===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''=== The first 624 experiments, including Carmen, were rounded up by [[Leroy]] and taken to a stadium to be destroyed. However, Lilo, Stitch, Jumba, Pleakley, Reuben, and Gantu arrived before the experiments could be destroyed. Carmen participated in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]], as in one scene, Carmen was seen strangling a Leroy. However, the Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe. ===''[[Stitch!]]''=== Carmen made an appearance in the ''Stitch!'' anime when [[Stitch]], [[Pleakley]], and [[Yuna Kamihara|Yuna]] travel to the past to the day Stitch was created. She was used to allow them to make their escape by making [[Dr. Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]] and his forces dance uncontrollably. It is shown that she does this by firing pink balls of energy out of her maracas. ==Trivia== *Carmen was first revealed in a pre-release promo image for ''[[Leroy & Stitch]]'' that was identical to the group photo at the end of the film. *Her name is a reference to {{WikipediaLink|Carmen Miranda}}, a world-famous [[Brazil]]ian singer and dancer of the early 20th century well known for wearing a headdress of tropical fruits and her use of maracas. *Carmen is one of the rare experiments to not have black eyes like most experiments, having light blue eyes instead. *She and [[Frenchfry]] are the only two known experiments who natively speak an Earth-based language other than English, with her being the only known Hispanophone ([[Spain|Spanish]]-speaking) experiment. *In a brief scene of ''Leroy & Stitch'' during the "[[Aloha ʻOe]]" concert, a towering, rather monstrous version of Carmen can be seen in the background. This version of her has a slightly elongated face; two long arms with larger hands and extended claws; a long, narrow torso; and what seems to be back spines that are extended similarly to [[Stitch]]'s spines. [[Experiments]] ("cousins")}} '''Bugby''', also known as '''Experiment 128''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. He is designed to turn entire civilizations into harmless insects. Those turned into bugs can understand all other insects and arachnids; only Jumba's technology can reverse the process. His one true place is on a farm, protecting farmers' crops by turning rocks into aphid-eating ladybugs. ==Background== ===Physical appearance=== Bugby is a light-green mosquito-like experiment with four purple eyes, four wings, and six teal legs. ===Powers and abilities=== Bugby can fire a purple laser from his stinger that causes individuals hit to turn into bugs and any giant insects and arachnids hit to revert to the normal size of bugs. Anyone turned into a bug can communicate with all other insects and arachnids. His ray can also, if reprogrammed, turn inanimate objects into bugs instead of living organisms. ===Weaknesses=== Only a special machine built by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] can reverse Bugby's effects. The machine can also enlarge normal-sized insects to the size of average human beings. ==Appearances== ===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''=== Experiment 128 was the 128th genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Dr. Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to turn people into harmless insects. 128 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch|Experiment 626]]. All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of Kauai, with 128's pod landing in the middle of a farm crop. When the crop was being irrigated via sprinklers, 128's pod was sprinkled, activating the experiment. 128 then took flight and traversed the island of Kauai aimlessly. After a while, 128 was attacked by an eagle but defeated it by turning it into a dragonfly. 128 then fluttered off laughing but accidentally flew into [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]]'s jar. Unaware that 128 was actually an experiment, Lilo named him Bugby and took him [[Lilo's House|home]], where she placed Bugby in her makeshift bug city, Bugopolis. When [[Stitch]] grabbed Bugby and attempted to eat him, the latter turned Stitch into an ant in self-defense. Later, after Lilo got in a fight with [[Nani Pelekai|Nani]] for bringing bugs into the house and was sent to her room, she noticed Bugby loose in her bedroom outside of Bugopolis and went to check on the other insects. Bugby then turned Lilo into a ladybug. Shortly after, [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] and [[Pleakley]] went up to Lilo's room to bring her gravel muffins (which Jumba deemed inedible), and the two discovered Bugby, making Pleakley become intrigued. When Jumba then tried to warn Pleakley about Bugby, the latter turned Jumba into a stink bug and Pleakley into a praying mantis. The four later befriended a [[Chaps, Manny, and Sperk|dung beetle, spider, and caterpillar]], though the bug trio believed Stitch was evil since he ate insects like them. However, Lilo convinced them otherwise, and when the three real bugs were in danger of insect-hating Nani and the exterminator, Stitch rescued them and eventually had a change of heart about eating bugs. After a few setbacks, including a tussle with an aggressive wild cat, the gang managed to travel to [[Jumba's Ship|Jumba's ship]], where they used a special machine to revert to normal (and enlarge the three real bugs to human size). When the exterminator showed up, thinking the vermin crawled into here, the giant bugs' leader told the exterminator off, scaring him away. Bugby then attacked, reverting the giant insects to their original size. However, Lilo and Stitch were able to recapture Bugby in Lilo's jar before he could turn her, Stitch, Jumba, and Pleakley back into bugs. Shortly after, Jumba reprogrammed Bugby to turn inanimate objects into bugs instead of people and sent the latter onto the same farm where he was first activated, where he found his one true place turning rocks into aphid-eating ladybugs, thus helping farmers protect their crops from unwanted pests. ===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''=== The first 624 experiments, including Bugby, were rounded up by [[Leroy]] and taken to a stadium to be destroyed. However, [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]], [[Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben]] and [[Captain Gantu|Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed. Bugby participated in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]] probably by turning attacking Leroys into insects. However, the Leroy clones soon gained the upper hand in the battle but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe. ==Gallery== {{Gallerylink}} ==Trivia== *Bugby, [[Babyfier]], [[Jam]], [[Melty]], [[Wishy-Washy]], [[Snooty]], [[Amnesio]], [[Hunkahunka]], [[Experiments#5-Series: Elemental and environmental manipulators|Blake]], [[Slugger]], [[Witch (Lilo & Stitch)|Witch]], and two [[Unconfirmed Experiments#Comic Zone Volume 1: Disney's Lilo & Stitch|unconfirmed]] [[Unconfirmed Experiments#Miscellaneous|experiments]] are the only known experiments that have wings. *Bugby, [[Plasmoid]], and [[Clink]] are the only known experiments that are hexapods. Interestingly, all three are different types of arthropods (insects, arachnids, and crustaceans respectively). *Bugby is one of the only experiments that Stitch didn't instantly recognize as a fellow cousin. *Bugby is one of the few known experiments whose powers Stitch is vulnerable to. **He is also one of the few known experiments whose powers Lilo falls victim to. *Bugby's [[Experiment Pods|pod]] color is purple. *In [[Bugby (episode)|his debut]], Bugby's eyes are purple, but in ''[[Leroy & Stitch]]'', they are black. *Bugby is one of the few experiments to not appear in the group photo at the end of ''Leroy & Stitch''. ==External links== *{{L&S|Bugby (128)}} {{Lilo & Stitch}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Bugby}} [[Category:Males]] [[Category:Aliens]] [[Category:Lilo & Stitch characters]] [[Category:Lilo & Stitch Experiments]] [[Category:Creatures]] [[Category:Disney characters]] [[Category:Bugs]] [[Category:Animated characters]] [[Category:Silent characters]]

He is designed to play practical jokes on unsuspecting victims. His one true place is performing an opening act for [[Moses Puloki|Moses]]' hula gig. ==Background== ===Personality=== PJ is incredibly silly and mischievous, even towards other experiments. Being an expert prankster, PJ uses his intelligence to create ingenious pranks. As [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]] describes, PJ can be annoying with his pranks, and while his pranks can be mean, he doesn't seem to be purposely malicious, but merely carries out his programming. Like most experiments, he dislikes it when his goals do not carry through or are interrupted. He likes making individuals laugh with his practical jokes. ===Physical appearance=== PJ is an orange and tan koala-like experiment with a white face and white belly, a wide mouth, red nose, black eyes, two thin yellow-tipped antennae on his head resembling rabbit-like ears, and a functioning blow-horn for a tail (reminiscent of {{WikipediaLink|Harpo Marx}}'s trademark horn), which he honks instead of speaking. He wears joke eyeglasses with a fake nose and mustache resembling those of {{WikipediaLink|Groucho Marx}}. ===Powers and abilities=== PJ is a skilled practical joker. He can play practical jokes by using his surroundings, various joke gags (e.g. hand buzzer, whoopee cushion, squirt flower, etc.), and other things he finds. ==Appearances== ===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''=== Experiment 133 was the 133rd genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Dr. Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to play practical jokes on victims, hence his name P(ractical) J(oker). 133 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch|Experiment 626]]. All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of Kauai. When a man using a metal detector on [[Lahui Beach|the beach]] uncovered an empty soda can with 133's pod, he decided that the pod wasn't worth anything, so he threw it into the water, activating the experiment. 133, named PJ (for Practical Joker), then proceeded to play practical jokes on everyone he could find. After a while, PJ ran into [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]] and [[Stitch]]. When PJ pulled many pranks on Stitch, the latter attempted to beat him up, only to be stopped by Lilo, who pointed out that the annoying prankster was still Stitch's cousin. PJ was later taken back to the [[Lilo's House|Pelekais' house]], where [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] claimed that PJ's jokes could result in mayhem. Regardless, PJ relentlessly pranked Lilo's strict substitute teacher for her [[Kaiāulu Hale|hula class]], while unknowingly framing Lilo for it. Later, Lilo wanted to play a spiteful joke on her harsh substitute teacher, despite Stitch's protests. PJ then pulled some more pranks on Stitch when the latter tried to capture him. However, Stitch eventually scooped PJ in a [[Prison Capsule|container]] so that he wouldn't cause further chaos. When Stitch refused to allow PJ to help with Lilo's scheme, she used [[Drowsy]] to put Stitch to sleep and released PJ from containment for his assistance. PJ then cleverly formulated a plan to humiliate Lilo's substitute teacher with the ultimate practical joke. Stitch somehow later woke up on his own and triggered a booby trap set up by PJ, resulting in Stitch getting stuck inside PJ's containment orb. The next morning, Stitch was freed from containment by [[Pleakley]]. The former then rushed to Lilo's hula school, hoping to prevent her and PJ from pulling their prank. Meanwhile, PJ waited to unleash his practical joke on Lilo's substitute teacher, which ended up backfiring (due to Stitch intervening), and thus caused PJ to literally get caught in his own trap. Luckily, PJ was freed from his own contraption by a sympathetic Stitch. Shortly after, PJ found his one true place as an opening act performer for [[Moses Puloki|Moses]]' hula gig. ===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''=== The first 624 experiments, including PJ, were rounded up by [[Leroy]] and taken to a stadium to be destroyed. However, [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]], [[Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben]], and [[Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed. PJ participated in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]]. The Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben, and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe. PJ joins them for the song by playing the trumpet. ===''[[Stitch!]]''=== PJ made an appearance in the ''Stitch!'' anime where he was released by [[Dr. Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]] to play practical jokes around town while disguised as [[Stitch]] in order to frame him for the pranks. In "Shogun", it is shown that PJ was dehydrated back into an experiment pod and locked in [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]]'s vault. PJ later appeared as one of the experiments who helped Stitch fight [[Dark End]]. He also appeared in the special ''Stitch and the Planet of Sand''. ==Gallery== {{Gallerylink}} ==Trivia== *Jumba refers to PJ as a "Practical joke gone mad! Unholy offspring of science and evil!" His "harmless little pranks soon become clever, medium-sized booby-traps, then extra-large dangerous sabotage, and then *makes explosion and siren noises* EVIL!" Though Jumba later admits that most of it was his own practical joke. *PJ's [[Experiment Pods|pod]] color is white. *In the group photo taken at the end of ''[[Leroy & Stitch]]'' and the Disney.com Lilo and Stitch experiment gallery, PJ is not wearing his glasses. [[Experiments]] ("cousins")}} '''Bragg''', also known as '''Experiment 145''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. Originally designed to annoy individuals by telling tall tales, he only appeared in the ''[[Stitch!]]'' anime where he was altered by [[Dr. Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]] to gain power from sympathy. He is an excellent liar, manipulator, and acts generally cute. He is also super-intelligent and talented with both the flute and harmonica, which assists in his gaining sympathy and popularity. He is capable of reaching strength that rivals that of [[Stitch]]'s. In the English dub, he is given the name '''Flute''' by [[Yuna Kamihara|Yuna]] and is correctly referred to as '''Experiment 145''', though the [[Japan]]ese language episode erroneously refers to Bragg as '''Experiment 021''', which actually belongs to '''Twang''', and mentions that Jumba reused some of Twang's DNA when he created Bragg. ==Background== Experiment 145 was the 145th genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Dr. Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to annoy individuals by telling tall tales. He inherited musical ability from Experiment 021, whose DNA was re-purposed in the creation of Experiment 145. He was later altered to feed off of sympathy and attention in order to grow stronger. 145 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch|Experiment 626]]. All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of Kauai. At an unknown point, 145 was activated during [[Lilo & Stitch: The Series|the original series]], although his outcome was never revealed. Many years later, he was captured by Hämsterviel, brainwashed, and modified to fool the citizens of Okinawa and capture Stitch. ===Personality=== Bragg acts like a conscientious, sensitive, and generous creature, but in reality is very manipulative and mischievous. He is a great actor, able to keep up an act for weeks. He is sly, able to come up with believable stories to get sympathy from other beings. Before being modified, Bragg was a mean, nasty, ogre-like brute with a gangster-like voice and a bad attitude, and was not very good at keeping his mouth shut. After his modification, despite his mischievous and destructive tendency, Bragg is still very friendly, fun-loving, and helpful and has a soft, sweet voice and a good attitude. ===Physical appearance=== In his original form, Bragg is not so cute and rather ogre-like. His fur was a vulgar shade of green, his claws extend, he had an under-bite, a bulbous red nose, a hunched back, and was overall very muscular. In his current/modified form, Bragg is a yellow long-eared cat/rabbit-like experiment with a white stomach and orange heart-shaped markings on his forehead and all down his back. He has blue tufts of fur sprouting from his ears, violet-colored eyes, and a reddish-orange nose. His tail is short and slightly bushy. As he grows stronger, he retains in his modified, yellow body, but becomes visibly muscular. At this stage, he possesses two retractable arms, and his voice gets deeper. He can switch between this and his first form at will to absorb more sympathy. ===Powers and abilities=== Bragg has musical talent and is able to play folksy instruments, such as a flute and harmonica, an ability he inherited from Jumba re-purposing Twang (021)'s DNA when creating Experiment 145. Bragg has superhuman intellect, able to work out complex problems in seconds (similar to Stitch), and is capable of speaking fluently. Aside from this, Bragg is deceptive, able to cause sympathy from any being. He is a highly skilled actor, which is one out of many reasons he is so popular. He uses popularity and sympathy as steroids, growing stronger as he receives more and more attention. This allows him to extend multiple arms, increase in size, and gain much physical muscle mass. He has been shown to have two retractable arms in his powered-up form (although it is unknown if he has retractable arms in his weaker form). ===Weaknesses=== If Bragg is disliked and his popularity decreases, he also decreases in strength and becomes very weak, stuck in his smaller form. ==Appearances== ===''[[Stitch!]]''=== This experiment first appeared when [[Yuna Kamihara|Yuna]] and [[Stitch]] found him crying in a picnic basket on the beach. After feeling sorry for him when he explains all the hardship he has been through, Yuna brings him home and eventually names him Flute, because he plays the flute. Flute appears to be sensitive and helpful at first, but when Stitch wakes up in the middle of the night and finds Flute eating all the food, Flute makes it look as if Stitch hurt him after he tried to stop Flute from being bad, thus getting Stitch in trouble. It turned out that [[Dr. Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]] altered Flute and disguised him, turning him from ugly to "snuggly-wuggly". This made him appear smaller, and his fur color changed from pale green to bright yellow to appeal to more people. He even became unrecognizable by his own creator, [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]]. He becomes physically stronger and mutates through getting attention, which he is fully capable of as he is a talented player of the harmonica and flute. He is shown to be very smart and athletic, making him very popular on only the first day he came with Yuna to school. Hämsterviel gave Flute the objective to reach his maximum power in order to capture Stitch so that [[Delia]] can get the power cell inside of him. Flute accomplishes this and beats on Stitch, but once he is caught and criticized by the townspeople, Flute loses his popularity, and thus his power, and he fails Hämsterviel miserably. [[Experiments]] ("cousins")}} '''Bonnie''', also known as '''Experiment 149''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. She is designed to be an expert in theft and evasion. She also has advanced lingual skills, enabling her to easily communicate with her partner-in-crime, [[Clyde (Lilo & Stitch)|Clyde]], whom she is programmed to be drawn to. Her one true place was originally in Kokaua Town Prison, but she was paroled in "[[Snafu (episode)|Snafu]]". After that, it is unknown where her one true place currently is. ==Background== ===Personality=== Bonnie is a {{WikipediaLink|Kleptomania|kleptomaniac}}. However, this doesn't stop her from being quite a helpful friend to others, such as [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]] and [[Stitch]] (after she was reformed), as seen in "[[Snafu (episode)|Snafu]]". Jumba programmed her to be drawn to her partner-in-crime, Clyde. Bonnie can be considered the brains and leader of the duo and is able to speak fluently. Bonnie has the qualities and characteristics of a true, albeit amateurish criminal mind: manipulative, cunning, street-smart, and a great schemer. She is normally quite laid-back in situations (unless maybe the cops or other enemies are after her). With such a carefree, social, and almost friendly personality, it can be quite easy for the gullible to fall for her rotten tricks, namely Lilo and Stitch. In addition to her deceptive, tomboyish nature, Bonnie appears to have little etiquette and be very rude, as well as a bit short-tempered at times. She has an extremely close bond with Clyde, despite the fact that they have argued a few times before. She is naturally just seeking thrill, fun, and adventure, even if it means stealing a few things or joining in on brawls with her other experiment "cousins". She and Clyde are also seen to be hoarders as well as thieves. ===Physical appearance=== Bonnie is a small, light green koala-like experiment with an hourglass-like figure and a large head. She has a yellow stomach, small antennae, dark blue eyes with eyelashes, two dark green marks on the back of her head, dark green arrow-like patches on her arms and legs, and a yellow V-shaped stripe on her forehead. She also has two fangs sticking out of her mouth. ===Powers and abilities=== Bonnie is cunning and intelligent with a talent for stealing things. She has some of the basic experiment abilities, such as enhanced durability and damage resistance, as well as having the ability to crawl on walls and ceilings. She is skilled with certain weapons, namely pistols and plasma guns. She can also speak fluently with a Brooklyn accent. Her connection to Clyde is programmed into her DNA. ==Appearances== ===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''=== Experiment 149 was the 149th genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Dr. Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. She was designed to work with Experiment 150 to steal many belongings and evade arrest. 149 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch|Experiment 626]]. All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of Kauai. 149 and 150's pods eventually made their way into a supply of doughnut holes at [[Kiki's Coffee Hut]]. While off duty, [[Officer Kahiko]] bought a bag containing two dozen doughnut holes at the coffee shack. He then took out 149 and 150's pods and (mistaking them for a new flavor) dipped them into his coffee, activating the two experiments, which proceeded to strip Kahiko and hijack his police car. The criminal duo next made a vain attempt to break into [[Gantu's Ship|Gantu's ship]], but were forced to flee the scene when [[Captain Gantu|Gantu]], who had been notified of their activation, caught them in the act. 149 and 150 went on to cause countless robberies throughout the island until they were tracked back to their hideout by [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]] and [[Stitch]], who had gone AWOL after being grounded by [[Nani Pelekai|Nani]] earlier. After getting acquainted with each other, 149 devised a plan to encourage Lilo and Stitch's unruly behavior so that they would eventually show the two experiments how to break into Gantu's ship. At first, Lilo and Stitch's naughty behavior posed as a distraction for 149 and 150 (named Bonnie and Clyde) while they stole from numerous places. The following night, Bonnie and Clyde managed to convince Lilo and Stitch to help them successfully break into Gantu's ship. However, before the four could steal anything, they were ambushed and captured in [[Prison Capsule|containment orbs]] by Gantu. Lilo and Stitch were able to break out, though, and the four made a narrow escape. When the outlaw experiments discovered that the police had found and secured their hideout, Bonnie convinced Lilo and Stitch to allow her and Clyde to take cover in the [[Lilo's House|Pelekais' house]]. Bonnie and Clyde attempted to hide in Lilo's laundry, but were discovered by [[Pleakley]] while the latter was taking out the laundry, prompting the two robbers to tie him and [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] up, unclothe them, and strip the house of everything. Jumba and Pleakley were later freed, and then let Lilo and Stitch use [[the Red One]] to chase down Bonnie and Clyde. While the two thieves fled to their new hideout in Nani's [[X-Buggy|dune buggy]] – along with all of the Pelekais' stolen possessions in tow – they were attacked by Gantu in his [[Manta Shuttle|shuttle]], but saved by Lilo and Stitch, whom Bonnie and Clyde took back to their new hideout: the pre-robbed coffee shack. However, Lilo and Stitch suddenly revealed their true colors: to re-infiltrate Bonnie and Clyde's hideout in order to capture them. When Stitch pointed a [[Net Cannon|net cannon]] at the two crooks, Bonnie and Clyde attempted to escape out a window that was locked, but were blasted into a net by Stitch, handed over to Officer Kahiko, and sent to prison. In "[[Spike (episode)|Spike]]", Bonnie was one of the experiments in Pleakley's E.A.R.W.A.X. group, alongside Clyde. When [[Fibber]] used his lie-detecting ability to prove that Bonnie was not as intelligent as she claimed, nor was Clyde at fault for their arrest, the duo got into a fight, which ended when Pleakley convinced Bonnie and Clyde to attempt hugging therapy on each other. In "[[Snafu (episode)|Snafu]]", Bonnie and Clyde were officially paroled, thus allowing them to join Lilo and Stitch on a mission to rescue Gantu's captive experiments. They assisted by opening a passage in Gantu's ship so Stitch and the others could break inside. ===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''=== The first 624 experiments, including Bonnie and Clyde, were rounded up by [[Leroy]] and taken to a stadium to be destroyed. However, [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]], [[Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben]], and [[Captain Gantu|Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed. Bonnie and Clyde participated in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]]. The Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle, but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben, and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe. ===''[[Stitch!]]''=== Bonnie and Clyde made an appearance in the ''Stitch!'' anime, where they escaped from Galactic Prison and traveled to the [[Izayoi Island|island]] in order to continue their primary function: theft. Because of this, they could be considered "incompletely rehabilitated". They have also revealed that they've tried to be good, but their programming interferes with it. Thus, it is unknown if they have truly turned good. ==Gallery== {{Gallerylink|Bonnie}} ==Trivia== *Bonnie is Experiment 149. However, in [[Bonnie & Clyde|her debut]], her [[Experiment Pods|pod]] is labeled 349, most likely due to Jumba's untidy [[Jumba's Computer|database]]. **She is also called 349 in the ''[[Stitch!]]'' anime and its English dub. *Bonnie is named after the bank robber, {{WikipediaLink|Bonnie and Clyde|Bonnie Parker}}. *She speaks fluently like [[Reuben]], but with a Brooklyn accent. **She is also one of the few known experiments that can speak fluently. **Additionally, she is shown to be more talkative than her partner, Clyde. *Bonnie is one of the rare experiments to not have black eyes like most experiments, having dark blue eyes instead. Interestingly, she shares this trait with [[Tickle-Tummy]], [[Welko]], and [[Witch (Lilo & Stitch)|Witch]], three other female experiments. *Bonnie normally has two fangs, but in "[[Spike (episode)|Spike]]", she was seen with six fangs (four on the top and two on the bottom). **In the same episode, [[Disney+]] closed captioning mistakenly shows Clyde to call her "Barney", probably mistranscribed due to his accent. *Bonnie's pod color is purple. *The [[Experiment Pod Container]] describes Bonnie as: "Experiment 149.
