Dream eater |home = [[Hawaii]] |likes = Turning dreams into nightmares |dislikes = Capture, being defeated |powers = Dream manipulation |status = Reprogrammed |creator = [[Jumba Jookiba]] |family = [[Experiments]] ("cousins")}} '''Remmy''', also known as '''Experiment 276''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. He is designed to infiltrate victims' dreams and transform them into nightmares. If the victim wakes up while Remmy is still inside, he will remain within his host's mind forever to turn all future dreams into nightmares. His one true place is at Kimo's Arcade, sending gamers into virtual realities of their fantasies after Jumba reprogrammed him. ==Background== ===Physical appearance=== Remmy is a light blue, floating ghostlike experiment with a huge head, a dark blue marking on top, little antennae, black eyes, and a thin mouth in a perpetual grin. ===Powers and abilities=== Remmy can cause nightmares by entering through a victim's ear and infiltrating their dreams. He is also designed to attack at the peak of the person's subconscious enjoyment. If the victim wakes up while he is still inside, 276 will remain there permanently to turn all future dreams into nightmares. ===Weaknesses=== If Remmy's host is reminded of something happy, the host will be able to turn the nightmare back into a dream, leaving Remmy weak and powerless. ==Appearances== ===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''=== Experiment 276 was the 276th genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Dr. Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to enter enemies' dreams and transform them into nightmares. 276 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch|Experiment 626]]. All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of Kauai, with 276's pod landing in a turtle's nest on [[Lahui Beach|the beach]]. When a sea turtle discovered 276's pod in its nest, it threw the pod out, which then landed in the path of an incoming tide, activating 276. Later, 276 traveled to the [[Lilo's House|Pelekai residence]], where, after [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]] settled down for a nap to cope with her grief (as it was the anniversary of [[Mr. and Mrs. Pelekai|her parents]]' death), he proceeded to invade Lilo's dreams. [[Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], and [[Pleakley]] entered Lilo's dreams to capture 276, who dissolved Lilo's initial dream and caused a chain reaction of dream sequences. When the four eventually had a chance, they tried to suck 276 up with a vacuum, but the latter was able to use a fire hydrant to block the nozzle. Angered at the four's attempt to capture him, 276 replaced Lilo's dream with a happier one, which later turned into a nightmare. [[Nani Pelekai|Nani]] soon came into Lilo's room to wake her up, only to be stopped by Pleakley, who had just exited the nightmares. He then explained that if Lilo awakens, 276 will remain inside her head forever and cause future nightmares. Nani sang Lilo a lullaby when the latter began stirring in her sleep. She then convinced Pleakley to re-enter Lilo's nightmare and show her a photo of their parents, believing it would help make her feel better. When the monsters in the nightmare eventually had Lilo, Stitch, and Jumba cornered, Pleakley re-entered Lilo's nightmare and then gave her the Pelekai family photo. Looking at it allowed Lilo to remember the happy times she and Nani had with their parents. Lilo's laughter destroyed the nightmare and defeated 276, rendering him powerless. He was shortly after captured and extracted by Jumba. 276, named Remmy, was then reprogrammed by Jumba to be completely harmless and given a one true place sending gamers at the local arcade into virtual realities of their fantasies, but without giving them nightmares. ===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''=== The first 624 experiments, including Remmy, were rounded up by [[Leroy]] and taken to a stadium to be destroyed. However, [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]], [[Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben]], and [[Captain Gantu|Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed. Remmy participated in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]]. The Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle, but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben, and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe. ===''[[Stitch!]]''=== Remmy has made two appearances in the ''Stitch!'' anime where he infiltrated both [[Yuna Kamihara|Yuna]] and [[Stitch]]'s dreams. His first appearance was in Season 2 in "A Recurring Nightmare". As it is explained later in the episode, Remmy was happy in his one true place in Kimo's Arcade in Kauai, but was eventually abandoned due to the decreasing popularity of video arcades in favor of video games at home. Because of this, he reverted back to his evil, nightmare-granting ways. He came to the island for revenge and despite Stitch trying to stop him, infiltrated Yuna's dreams. [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] decides to send Stitch, [[Pleakley]], and [[BooGoo]] into Yuna's dream to get Remmy out before Yuna wakes up and they're all trapped inside her dreams forever. Eventually, the group reaches the location where Remmy has his base set up. After getting inside, he challenges everyone to a quiz show, using Yuna's memories as the questions. After a few easy questions, he asks for the lullaby that Yuna's deceased mother used to sing to her when she was a baby. Unfortunately, Yuna doesn't remember, so they lose the game. Remmy sends the group to three different locations in his base to play "virtual reality" games to make up for losing the quiz show. He sends Stitch to a racing game, Pleakley to a shooting game, and Yuna and BooGoo to a zombie-fighting game. Stitch and Pleakley both lose their games and wake up. Remmy and BooGoo are still in the dream, however, so Stitch, Jumba, and later Pleakley all go back to Yuna's dream to help. Seeing her treasured ''[[Pelekai ʻohana|ʻohana]]'' fighting alongside her, Yuna gains control of her dream, giving Stitch the power to defeat all the enemies and weakening Remmy enough for Jumba to capture him. Remmy regrets his actions and makes up for it by showing Yuna her deepest memory: her mother's face and lullaby. As Yuna starts to wake up, Remmy's base collapses, so Stitch, Pleakley, Jumba, BooGoo, and Remmy all leave Yuna's dream. In the morning, however, Remmy still needs someone to give nightmares to, so Jumba sends him to [[Dr. Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]] to turn his dreams into nightmares. In his second appearance, Remmy is released by Hämsterviel to give Stitch nightmares so that [[Captain Gantu|Gantu]] and [[Reuben]] can have the chance to capture him and send him back to Hämsterviel. Therefore, Yuna and Jumba have to go inside Stitch's dreams while Pleakley keeps Stitch from waking up or becoming too agitated from the nightmares. They manage to capture Remmy at the last second before Gantu and Reuben can transport him. ==Gallery== {{Gallerylink}} ==Trivia== *His name is a reference to the {{WikipediaLink|Rapid eye movement sleep|REM stage of sleep}} in which dreams occur (REM means Rapid Eye Movement). *Remmy resembles the [[w:c:pacman:Ghosts|ghosts]] from the ''[[w:c:pacman:Pac-Man (series)|Pac-Man]]'' video game series (particularly [[w:c:pacman:Inky|Inky]] in terms of color). *Remmy, [[Phantasmo]], [[Fudgy]], [[Tickle-Tummy]], and [[Witch (Lilo & Stitch)|Witch]] are the only known experiments to have arms but no legs. **Interestingly, excluding Fudgy, all of these experiments are capable of levitation. Remmy is always seen levitating. Phantasmo and Witch primarily levitate but often possess objects or living beings to move by other means. Tickle-Tummy is also able to levitate, but has been seen bouncing as well. *Remmy's [[Experiment Pods|pod]] color is green. ==External links== *{{L&S|Remmy (276)}} {{Lilo & Stitch}} [[Category:Lilo & Stitch characters]] [[Category:Lilo & Stitch Experiments]] [[Category:Aliens]] [[Category:Males]] [[Category:Monsters]] [[Category:Creatures]] [[Category:Disney characters]] [[Category:Animated characters]] [[Category:Silent characters]] [[Category:Stitch! characters]]

Flight |status = Active |creator = [[Jumba Jookiba]] |family = [[Experiments]] ("cousins") |owner = [[Victoria]]}} '''Snooty''', also known as '''Experiment 277''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. He is designed to mine and enrich Snootonium, a rare intergalactic energy source that becomes unstable and dangerous once enriched. Luckily, there is none on Earth, which [[Captain Gantu|Gantu]] sees as no reason to capture Snooty, only doing so under [[Dr. Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s orders. However, Snootonium has a similar chemical composition to mucus, and thus his programming draws him to individuals with large quantities. His one true place is as [[Victoria]]'s pet, clearing her sinuses. ==Background== ===Personality=== Snooty is a single-minded experiment dedicated to mining and enriching Snootonium. There is none on Earth, but Snootonium has a similar chemical composition to mucus, so his programming draws him to individuals with large quantities of mucus, such as Victoria and [[Stitch]] (his body is 62.7% mucus). Unlike most experiments, Snooty is not inherently vile and is one of the tamer experiments that will avoid harming others in his search. However, he will defend himself if he is provoked and is very persistent in fulfilling his primary function. ===Physical appearance=== Snooty is a vampire-esque experiment resembling a light-purple bat. He has a furless, triangle-shaped body and pointed ears. He has stumpy legs and dark purple wings each with two fingers and a thumb. He hardly has a neck, but in place is a wide fanged mouth. ===Powers and abilities=== To detect Snootonium, Snooty sees in an unidentified vision spectrum that allows him to detect the substance (similar to how snakes' infrared vision allows them to detect body heat). Snooty can also mine and enrich Snootonium and/or mucus by using his mouth/fangs; in the latter's case, he retrieves it via sucking it from a victim's nostrils in seconds. ==Appearances== ===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''=== Experiment 277 was the 277th genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Dr. Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to mine and enrich Snootonium, a rare element that has a similar chemical composition as Earth mucus. 277 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch|Experiment 626]]. All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of Kauai. 277's pod eventually made its way onto a pickup truck's antenna. When the owner took the dirty pickup through a car wash, the pod got wet in the wash, activating the experiment. After spooking the pickup's driver, 277 left in search of mucus (considering the fact that there was no Snootonium available on Earth). Drawn by her allergies, 277 frequently attacked [[Victoria]], who mistook him for a real vampire, but each time he was warded off by [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]] and [[Stitch]]. They also prevented an impetuous [[Captain Gantu|Gantu]] from capturing the experiment, despite Victoria's protests. When Lilo later looked up 277 on [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]]'s [[Jumba's Computer|computer]], she informed Victoria that 277 was not an actual vampire and didn't need to be slain or feared once rehabilitated, although Victoria remained wary. Later, when Lilo and Victoria were out looking for 277, named Snooty, he made another attempt on Victoria, prompting her to hide in [[Officer Kahiko]]'s police car. During this assault, Stitch bravely challenged the bat-like experiment. Snooty, upon detecting the visible mucus in Stitch's body, attacked the latter and sucked him dry. After Snooty put Stitch out of commission, Victoria vowed to slay the former if she had to do it without Lilo's help. When Lilo brought a weak and fatigued Stitch [[Lilo's House|home]], Jumba explained that Stitch's body was 62.7% mucus that had been drained out, temporarily weakening him. Jumba then revealed that mucus had a chemical composition similar to Snootonium, despite it being unavailable on Earth. This also explained why Snooty kept going after Victoria. Meanwhile, Victoria was in a hardware store looking for items to slay Snooty with. She then noticed Gantu using the store's TV set (since [[Dr. Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]] had supposedly cut Gantu's cable service earlier according to [[Reuben|Experiment 625]]) and decided to team up with him to slay the experiment. Using Gantu's [[Manta Shuttle|shuttle]], the two tracked Snooty down to his cave in the [[Hawaii]]an mountains, where Gantu used Victoria as bait to successfully draw Snooty out. Lilo soon arrived with [[Pleakley]] and was shocked to see Victoria consorting with Gantu. She claimed that Gantu was helping her slay Snooty, but Lilo managed to convince Victoria of his treachery. Gantu blasted Snooty into a [[Net Cannon|net]], but the latter was then saved by Victoria and Lilo, who both fought Gantu for the experiment. After being freed, Snooty rested contentedly in Victoria's arms. When Snooty used his mucus-sucking power to clear Victoria's sinuses, the latter kept him as a pet. ===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''=== In the film's opening, Snooty can be seen waving hello to [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]], along with [[Babyfier]] and [[Amnesio]]. Later, the first 624 experiments, including Snooty, were rounded up by [[Leroy]] and taken to a stadium to be destroyed. However, Lilo, [[Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben]], and [[Captain Gantu|Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed. Snooty participated in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]] by dodging Leroys' plasma projectiles and possibly draining Leroys' mucus. However, the Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle, but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben, and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe. ==Gallery== {{Gallerylink}} ==Trivia== *Snooty is an obvious parody of {{WikipediaLink|Count Dracula}} and vampires in general, except that vampires suck people's blood. *Snooty, [[Bugby]], [[Babyfier]], [[Jam]], [[Melty]], [[Wishy-Washy]], [[Amnesio]], [[Hunkahunka]], [[Experiments#5-Series: Elemental and environmental manipulators|Blake]], [[Slugger]], [[Witch (Lilo & Stitch)|Witch]], and two [[Unconfirmed Experiments#Comic Zone Volume 1: Disney's Lilo & Stitch|unconfirmed]] [[Unconfirmed Experiments#Miscellaneous|experiments]] are the only known experiments that have wings. *Snooty and Jam are the only known experiments based on bats. Interestingly, they are both in the 2-series and shades of purple. *Victoria initially mistook Snooty for a real vampire, thus fearing him and wanting him dead. *Snooty is one of the few known experiments whose powers Stitch is vulnerable to. *Snooty is the first and only known experiment that Victoria caught. *He is also one of the six known experiments to be rehabilitated by someone other than Lilo and Stitch, the other five being [[Gigi]], [[Elastico]], [[Yaarp]], [[Spike (Lilo & Stitch)|Spike]], and [[Frenchfry]]. **Snooty, in particular, was rehabilitated by Victoria. *Snooty's [[Experiment Pods|pod]] color is red. However, a white pod labeled 277 appeared among other pods in "[[Mrs. Hasagawa's Cats]]". *The [[Experiment Pod Container]] describes Snooty as: "Experiment 277. Primary function: Mine and enrich Snootonium." **He is the only known experiment whose above primary function is incapable of being utilized on Earth, as Snootonium is a substance not found on Earth. ==External links== *{{L&S|Snooty (277)}} {{Lilo & Stitch}} [[Category:Lilo & Stitch Experiments]] [[Category:Lilo & Stitch characters]] [[Category:Aliens]] [[Category:Creatures]] [[Category:Monsters]] [[Category:Bats]] [[Category:Males]] [[Category:Disney characters]] [[Category:Pets]] [[Category:Silent characters]] [[Category:Neutral characters]] [[Category:Vampires]]

[[Experiments]] ("cousins")}} '''Lax''', also known as '''Experiment 285''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. He is designed to halt the activity of entire work forces, companies, and innocent civilians by turning them lackadaisical with a zap from his antenna, causing civilizations to fail and making it easier to invade their planet, and it even works on technology. His one true place is at the [[Kauai Airport|local airport]], making grouchy tourists enjoy their vacation. ==Background== ===Physical appearance=== Lax is a purple parrot-like experiment with black eyes, a single green-tipped, [https://www.britannica.com/science/esca esca]-like antenna, a blue-striped beak, and green-striped tail feathers. ===Powers and abilities=== Lax can emit a green laser from his antenna that contains a chemical that relieves the sympathetic nervous system and causes the brain to deny stress, and therefore makes the victim feel "on vacation"; if the laser hits a machine, the chemical has a similar effect and causes all complex functions or artificial intelligence to shut off, creating the "vacation" effect. Thus, a person hit with Lax's ray will relax, and a machine hit with said ray will shut down. ==Appearances== ===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''=== Experiment 285 was the 285th genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Dr. Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to fire a green laser from his antenna that causes enemies, innocent civilians, and even modern technology to abandon work. 285 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch|Experiment 626]]. All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of Kauai, with 285's pod landing in some bushes near the [[Lilo's House|Pelekais' house]]. The [[Recess|Recess gang]], along with their chaperone [[Muriel Finster|Miss Finster]], accompany [[Gretchen Grundler|Gretchen]] to [[Hawaii]] after she makes a big discovery about a new planet. Meanwhile, [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]] and [[Stitch]], a local and her alien friend, have made a mess trying to create a new recipe. Lilo's older sister, [[Nani Pelekai|Nani]], orders them to clean it up and then leaves for work (however, while driving over a puddle, Experiment 285's pod was activated). Instead, they try to make [[Pleakley]], another alien with a love of cleaning, do it. However, after seeing how huge the mess is, Pleakley faints. Sometime after, Stitch wanders outside and does nothing except lie in a hammock. Then, Pleakley is zapped by the same unknown energy that got Stitch, causing him to laze about in a similar fashion. The same goes for another alien named [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], who just arrived. It turns out the culprit is Experiment 285, or Lax, an alien experiment with an antenna-like appendage that is designed to cause people to be very relaxed and lazy. Lilo and a lazy Stitch chase after him but instead find [[Ashley Spinelli|Spinelli]] running towards the pool of the [[Birds of Paradise Hotel|hotel]], followed closely by the rest of the Recess gang. Lilo follows as well, but then [[Mikey Blumberg|Mikey]] and [[Vince LaSalle|Vince]] (though at separate times) are zapped by Lax. Lilo explains everything to [[TJ Detweiler|T.J.]], and they then try to capture Lax, but they fail and he escapes. Meanwhile, [[Captain Gantu|Gantu]] is made to follow a satellite's directions to find Lax for the evil [[Dr. Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]. Lilo and four of the Recess characters, [[Gus Griswald|Gus]], T.J., Gretchen, and Spinelli, catch up to Lax at an observatory. T.J. and Spinelli try to get Lax themselves, but they too get zapped. Just then, Gretchen finds the new "planet" that she discovers, but Lilo finds out it's only a satellite being used by Hämsterviel (the same one Gantu uses). Gretchen's Galileo computer is zapped; however, Gretchen gets the idea to use the telescope to zap the satellite. While most of the Recess gang distract Lax by hitting golf balls at him, Gretchen is zapped, but she still works on the plan; apparently, she finds work relaxing. Gus gets chased by Lax, but Lilo distracts Lax just in time for Stitch to pummel him. Lilo, Gretchen, and Gus then put their plan into action, and the satellite ends up destroyed. Gantu confronts them, but Lax zaps him, thus ending the threat. The Recess gang eventually goes back to normal, and Lax finds a hobby in zapping stressed and unpleasant tourists at the [[Kauai Airport|airport]]. Then Spinelli wonders where Miss Finster is. It turns out Miss Finster has never left the spa. ===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''=== The first 624 experiments, including Lax, were rounded up by [[Leroy]] and taken to a stadium to be destroyed. However, [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]], [[Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben]], and [[Captain Gantu|Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed. Lax participated in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]] probably by making attacking Leroys lackadaisical. However, the Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle, but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben, and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe. ==Gallery== {{Gallerylink}} ==Trivia== *Lilo and Gus are the only main characters to not get zapped by Lax. *Lax is one of the few known experiments whose powers Stitch is vulnerable to. *There are a few moments between T.J. and Spinelli, like when he asked her to help him out with distracting the experiment Lax. Also, when the six kids plus Lilo and Stitch were all at the observatory, right before the two of them both get zapped by Lax, Spinelli is seen quickly taking T.J. by the hand and then running up together to the rooftop of the building. After that, they are both seen goofing off together on the beach, while under Lax's spell. *Lax's [[Experiment Pods|pod]] color is green. *Lax, [[Morpholomew]], and [[Spats]] are the only experiments that debuted in crossovers. *The [[Experiment Pod Container]] describes Lax as: "Experiment 285. Primary function: Causes enemies to abandon work." *Lax is one of the few experiments to not appear in the group photo at the end of ''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''. ==External links== *{{L&S|Lax (285)}} |-|Lilo & Stitch= {{Lilo & Stitch}} |-|Recess= {{Recess}} [[Category:Recess characters]] [[Category:Lilo & Stitch characters]] [[Category:Disney characters]] [[Category:Aliens]] [[Category:Males]] [[Category:Lilo & Stitch Experiments]] [[Category:Monsters]] [[Category:Creatures]] [[Category:Animated characters]] [[Category:Silent characters]]

He is designed to be a living boomerang as his name implies. His one true place is with [[Mrs. Hasagawa]] as one of her "cats". ==Appearances== ===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''=== Experiment 288 was the 288th genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Dr. Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to act as a living boomerang. 288 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture Experiment 626. All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of Kauai. Against statistically unlikely (but not impossible) odds, several experiment pods landed in one location: [[Mrs. Hasagawa]]'s yard, 288's pod being one of them. At an unknown point, [[Mrs. Hasagawa]] mistook 288's for an apricot and washed it, activating the experiment. However, as 288 was not a very evil or destructive experiment, he was able to live a peaceful life with her, due to the latter seeing the former as a mere stray cat who needed a home. When [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]] and [[Stitch]] discovered that Mrs. Hasagawa kept several experiments as pets, they thought they were a danger to her and along with [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] and [[Pleakley]], tried to capture them all. Stitch tried to get 288 to willingly go into a [[Prison Capsule|container]], but when he saw [[Mulch|Experiment 111]] rapidly approaching, he grabbed 288, threw him into the air, and used the aforementioned container on 111 instead. When 288 came back (the way real boomerangs do after being thrown), Stitch grabbed another container and caught him in it. 288 and the other experiments were about to be taken away, but were returned to Mrs. Hasagawa when Lilo and Stitch saw how much she cared for them. 288 was then named Boomer. In "[[Woops (episode)|Woops]]", Boomer was oddly seen as one of the captive experiments in [[Dr. Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s [[Prison Asteroid K-37|prison cell]], although he is barely seen, suggesting [[Captain Gantu|Gantu]] caught Boomer, but this was an error. Boomer was then sent back to Gantu after [[Woops|Experiment 600]] caused mischief and nearly blew Hämsterviel's cover to the [[UGF Troopers|prison guards]]. ===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''=== The first 624 experiments, including Boomer, were rounded up by Leroy and taken to a stadium to be destroyed. However, [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]], [[Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben]], and [[Captain Gantu|Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed. Boomer participated in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]] by being thrown at Leroys' heads. However, the Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle, but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben, and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe. ===''[[Stitch!]]''=== Boomer made an appearance in the ''Stitch!'' anime along with [[Pix]], [[Slushy]], [[Blowhard]], [[Kixx]], and [[Slugger]], when [[Yuna Kamihara|Yuna]] and [[Stitch]] visited [[Tokyo Disneyland]]. ==Trivia== *Boomer was activated off-screen. *In "[[Woops (episode)|Woops]]", Boomer erroneously appeared with Gantu's other captive experiments, although he is barely seen, but he was already living with Mrs. Hasagawa, and Lilo and Stitch discovered him while Gantu was asleep. ==Gallery== ===Screenshots=== L&S - 2x23A - Mrs. Hasagawa's Cats 13.png Manners greets his guests.png L&S - 2x23A - Mrs. Hasagawa's Cats 26.png L&S - 2x23A - Mrs. Hasagawa's Cats 27.png L&S - 2x23A - Mrs. Hasagawa's Cats 29.png L&S - 2x23A - Mrs. Hasagawa's Cats 33.png L&S - 2x23A - Mrs. Hasagawa's Cats 78.png L&S - 2x23A - Mrs. Hasagawa's Cats 80.png Boomer flies into container.png L&S - 2x23A - Mrs. Hasagawa's Cats 84.png Vlcsnap-2012-07-10-16h15m29s176.png Vlcsnap-2013-03-14-10h16m50s180.png Stitch! Amusement park ride |home = [[Hawaii]] |likes = Shorting out machines, being an amusement park ride (as a giant) |dislikes = Capture, defeat, being small |powers = Machine and electronics sabotaging |paraphernalia = Claws (pincers) |status = Active |creator = [[Jumba Jookiba]] |family = [[Experiments]] ("cousins")}} '''Shortstuff''', also known as '''Experiment 297''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. He is designed to sabotage mechanical devices; specifically, he is naturally drawn to electrical machinery, which he then shorts out to create utter chaos. Due to him being accidentally enlarged, his one true place is as a carnival ride. ==Background== ===Personality=== Shortstuff is shown to be short-tempered, reckless, and clever. Armed with four pincers, he is not exactly afraid to take on bigger opponents. He also seems to be quite tolerant of his enormous size after he was accidentally enlarged. As a giant, he was still able to wreak havoc and overpower an equally giant [[Stitch]] in battle. When Shortstuff was tamed and became a carnival ride after his defeat, he didn't seem to mind at all. ===Physical appearance=== Shortstuff is a small, red-orange crab-like experiment with four pincer-like claws, four spindle legs, dark blue eyes, a thin mouth with a turquoise tongue, and two small antennae on his head. Originally the size of a crab, he was accidentally enlarged to twice the size of a house. ===Powers and abilities=== Shortstuff can sabotage machinery by entering and then cutting the mechanism's electrical wiring using his claws, thus short-circuiting the appliance. He is also able to swivel at the waist more than 360 degrees. At his giant size, Shortstuff could overpower an equally giant Stitch in battle. ==Appearances== ===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''=== Experiment 297 was the 297th genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Dr. Hamsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to sabotage mechanical devices. 297 and the other first 625 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch|Experiment 626]]. All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of Kauai, with 297's pod landing in a sewage pipe. [[Stitch]] (in his "Kenny" disguise) was too short to participate in any of the carnival rides, so [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]] tried to treat him to some lemonade instead. However, when the vendor offended Stitch about his size, the latter broke the vendor's lemonade cart. When lemonade from the broken cart trickled into the pipe, it touched 297's pod, activating the experiment. [[Captain Gantu|Gantu]], who was at the amusement park with [[Reuben|Experiment 625]], criticized the carnival games, while Reuben was having fun winning prizes and later attempted to eat a colossal submarine sandwich, but Gantu thwarted him. Gantu suddenly saw 297 and grabbed him, but the latter was able to escape by simply pinching Gantu. While 297 likely began his rampage, Stitch, who wanted to be bigger than his normal size, rummaged through [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]]'s devices. Since Jumba was away doing community service, Lilo allowed [[Pleakley]] to enlarge Stitch with Jumba's [[Protoplasmic Growth Ray|growth ray]]. Unfortunately, during Stitch's growth process, Gantu came to the [[Lilo's House|Pelekai residence]] looking for 297, whom Lilo lied about capturing. Gantu then saw a humongous Stitch towering over him after he overconfidently compared his vast size to Lilo's. When she explained what had happened and threatened to make Stitch even bigger, Gantu was forced to retreat. Later, 297 had proceeded to sabotage every ride at the amusement park before being chased by Lilo and Stitch, the latter having great difficulty due to his enormous size that made him unbalanced. 297 was then captured in a [[Prison Capsule|containment orb]] and taken back to the house, where Lilo named him Shortstuff (because he liked to short out stuff). While Stitch was asleep on the couch, Lilo convinced Pleakley to shrink him back to his normal size. Unfortunately, while Pleakley fired up Jumba's growth ray, Shortstuff was able to use his claws to escape containment and attempted to sabotage the device. However, in the process, the ray enlarged Shortstuff into a behemoth just as he fled outside. Stitch then requested to be enlarged into an equal behemoth so he could take on Shortstuff. Meanwhile, a humongous Shortstuff resumed his rampage at the carnival, where he engaged an equally gigantic Stitch in battle. At first, Shortstuff was able to easily overpower Stitch, but after Jumba arrived and shrunk Stitch back to his normal, functional size with the shrink ray, the latter easily defeated Shortstuff, who was restrained with ropes. Shortstuff's size was never reverted, and as a result, he found his one true place as an amusement park ride, which Lilo and Stitch got to try out. ===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''=== The first 624 experiments, including Shortstuff, were rounded up by [[Leroy]] and taken to a stadium to be destroyed. However, [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]], [[Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben]], and [[Captain Gantu|Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed. Shortstuff participated in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]] by swatting attacking Leroys with his huge claws until a bunch of Leroys ensnared Shortstuff, causing him to fall over. However, the Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle, but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben, and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe. ===''[[Stitch!]]''=== Shortstuff made a cameo appearance in the ''[[Stitch!]]'' anime as an image on a computer screen (where he was shown to be at his normal size). [[Dr. Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]] was going to unleash him on the [[Izayoi Island|island]], but [[Captain Gantu|Gantu]] somehow confused Shortstuff's number (297) with [[Wishy-Washy]]'s number (267) and accidentally sent the latter instead. ==Gallery== {{Gallerylink}} ==Trivia== *Shortstuff is one of the rare experiments to not have black eyes like most experiments, having dark blue eyes instead. *Shortstuff, [[Ploot]], [[Clink]], [[Gotchu]], and two [[Unconfirmed Experiments#Leroy & Stitch|unconfirmed]] [[Unconfirmed Experiments#Comic Zone Volume 1: Disney's Lilo & Stitch|experiments]] are the only known experiments that have claws/pincers. Amorphous physiology |status = Active |creator = [[Jumba Jookiba]] |family = [[Experiments]] ("cousins")}} '''Spooky''', also known as '''Experiment 300''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. He is designed to terrify entire populations into submission by morphing into their worst fears; his forms are distinguishable by his glowing green eyes and hissing voice. His one true place is scaring trick-or-treaters on Halloween and (for the rest of the year) haunting the old, abandoned mansion. ==Background== ===Personality=== Spooky causes chaos by fulfilling the purpose he was programmed for: terrifying his enemies by turning into their worst fears. However, he went further by directly harming his victims, aside from just scaring them, and seems to be more dangerous than most experiments. Originally malicious and slightly sadistic, he often chooses to not only provoke fear in his victims, but also cause other mental trauma such as sadness and terror. He tends to slither and hiss like a snake, despite his most common form of being a blob. When victims are brave enough to stand up against his scares, Spooky becomes annoyed and apparently powerless against them. However, after being reformed, Spooky only scares individuals for fun on Halloween. He is also loyal and helpful to his friends, joining [[Stitch]]'s rebellion to fight off [[Captain Gantu|Gantu]]. ===Physical appearance=== Spooky's default form is a green blob-like experiment with glowing, olive-green eyes, a wide mouth with a turquoise tongue, two stubby arms and legs, and three round, stubby spikes on his back. When he changes into other forms, the mimics, as convincing as they appear, are distinguishable by his glowing green eyes and hissing voice. Spooky also appears to have a monstrous, secondary form assumed for combat and intimidation purposes. In this form, he is larger than normal, his spines grow longer, he gains eye stalks and claws, and his mouth becomes a reptilian jaw with jagged teeth. According to [[Stitch's Great Escape!]], the form is called "Spookymorp". ===Powers and abilities=== Spooky can shapeshift into his victims' deepest, darkest fears by taking the form of any person, animal, or object. He can also transform into substances other than solid objects, such as water or a twister. Spooky's body also gives him slime-like properties, for he can slither like a snake and turn elastic when moving. In the ''[[Stitch!]]'' anime, it is also revealed that Spooky has some limited form of telepathy to read his victims' thoughts and discover their worst fears after being transmutated by [[Dr. Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]. ==Appearances== ===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''=== Experiment 300 was the 300th genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Dr. Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to terrorize his victims by morphing into their worst fears. 300 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch|Experiment 626]]. All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of Kauai, with 300's pod landing on a house roof. On Halloween night, a gust of wind caused 300's pod to roll down the roof's rain gutter and into a rain barrel, activating the experiment. 300 then noticed a mouse and scared it off by turning into a wild cat. When a dog attacked 300 because of the cat form, the latter frightened the dog away by turning into a dogcatcher, then fled the scene in his elastic form. Shortly after, 300 attacked a children's Halloween party held at [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]]'s [[Kaiāulu Hale|school]], scaring [[Mertle Edmonds|Mertle]] and [[Elena, Teresa, and Yuki|the hula girls]] off by turning into a headless Lilo, then terrifying [[Moses Puloki|Moses]] by turning into a giant spider. Presumably after this, 300 lurked somewhere inside and waited for his next victim. Lilo and [[Stitch]] later arrived to discover the party in disarray. When Stitch entered the kitchen to raid the fridge, 300 locked himself in the kitchen with Stitch and almost drowned the latter by turning into floodwaters. However, 300 was forced to retreat up through an air vent when Lilo noticed his presence, relieving Stitch. Sometime later, 300 arrived at the [[Lilo's House|Pelekais' house]], where he terrified [[Nani Pelekai|Nani]] by turning into [[Cobra Bubbles]] and claiming he had come to take Lilo away. However, when Lilo and Stitch returned to the home and noticed Cobra to be 300 from his hissing voice, they exposed 300, named Spooky, as an impostor, thus forcing him to slip away again. Lilo, Stitch, [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], and [[Pleakley]] followed Spooky into the abandoned mansion, where he surprised and terrorized Lilo by turning into a clown. Lilo's shriek startled Stitch so much, he unintentionally fell into an indoor swimming pool. Spooky then chased after Lilo in his clown form, scaring her to the point where she clung to a high pillar screaming for help. While Spooky left Lilo and Stitch to their fate, the latter attempted to save Lilo, but he lost his grip on the pool's diving board and sank to the bottom. However, he overcame his aquaphobia by singing "[[Aloha ʻOe]]" (a song that Lilo taught him as a coping tactic), and after emerging from the pool, he managed to rescue Lilo in the nick of time. Meanwhile, Spooky defeated Jumba and Pleakley by turning into their worst fears: [[Mrs. Pleakley|Pleakley's mom]] and Jumba's ex-wife, but Stitch eventually saw and attacked Spooky's latter form. When Spooky noticed that Stitch had successfully faced his fears, and was thus undaunted by any other scary transformations, the former turned into a bat and attempted to escape up the chimney, but was ambushed and captured in a [[Prison Capsule|containment orb]] by Stitch. Spooky then found his one true place scaring trick-or-treaters on Halloween and (on other occasions) haunting the old, abandoned house. In "[[The Asteroid]]", Spooky was one of the six experiments that Stitch convinced to come with him and Lilo to save Earth from an approaching asteroid (Spooky briefly morphed into one to clarify). Along the journey, [[Kixx]] kicked the back of Spooky's seat, causing the latter (using his nightmarish morphing ability) to retaliate. Spooky later attempted to use a monstrous form to scare Pleakley into giving him free soda, but Pleakley only replied with an order for Spooky to return to his seat. Spooky was one of the experiments in "[[Checkers (episode)|Checkers]]" that joined Stitch in a rebellion against [[Captain Gantu|Gantu]]. Spooky even morphed into Gantu for clarification, then later morphed into a spiky, sea urchin-like fruit when the ex-captain was about to bite into him. ===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''=== The first 624 experiments, including Spooky, were rounded up by [[Leroy]] and taken to a stadium to be destroyed. However, [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]], [[Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben]], and [[Captain Gantu|Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed. Spooky participated in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]] by using nightmarish forms to scare Leroys. However, the Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle, but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben, and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe. ===''[[Stitch!]]''=== Spooky made an appearance in the ''Stitch!'' anime where he was released by [[Dr. Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]] along with [[Toons]] to scare the children of a summer camp. It is revealed that he uses a form of telepathy to read his victim's mind and discover their worst fears. In "Shogun", it is shown that Spooky was dehydrated back into an experiment pod and locked in [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]]'s vault. Eventually, Jumba grabbed his pod to help [[Stitch]] in his fight against [[Dark End]], but Spooky wasn't one of the experiments that was activated. ==[[Disney Experiences|Disney Parks]]== Spooky makes a cameo in the pre-show of [[Stitch's Great Escape!]] when [[Captain Gantu|Gantu]] shows guests a quick look at the "criminals" of the galaxy (which are all experiments). However, he does not appear in his true form, but rather the form he used on [[Pleakley]] shown in "[[The Asteroid]]". Underneath the image, his name is rendered as "300M/Spookymorp" (presumably meant to be "Spookymorp''h''") in [[Tantalog language|Tantalog]]. ==Gallery== {{Gallerylink}} ==Trivia== *Spooky was first revealed in a DVD bonus feature of ''[[Stitch! The Movie]]'' in the experiment gallery. *Spooky is one of the rare experiments to not have black eyes like most experiments, having glowing, olive-green eyes instead. *Spooky is one of the few known experiments whose powers Stitch is vulnerable to. **He is also one of the few known experiments whose powers Lilo falls victim to. *Spooky and [[Morpholomew]] are the only known experiments that have shapeshifting/transforming abilities. *Spooky is shown to have the ability to speak, although he appears to be only capable of speaking fluently when shapeshifting into something that can talk. *Jumba referred to Spooky as "X-300" (ex three hundred) and mentions that his impression of Jumba's ex-wife is frightening. **Disney has used "X-" (X with a hyphen) in promotional material as a shorthand prefix for "Experiment". *Unlike most experiments, Spooky's number is pronounced as a whole number ("three hundred") instead of three individual digits (which in his case would have been "three-oh-oh") as per the norm for the experiments. **The only other experiment seen in [[Lilo & Stitch: The Series|the original series]] whose number is also referred to as a whole number is [[Woops]] (Experiment 600). [[Experiments]] ("cousins")}} '''Amnesio''', also known as '''Experiment 303''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. He is designed to erase his victims' memories with a red laser vision from his eyes. Luckily, Jumba programmed a password into him to reverse the amnesia process, though it must be spoken within earshot of him. He was captured by [[Captain Gantu|Gantu]], but was rescued in "[[Snafu (episode)|Snafu]]". ==Background== ===Physical appearance=== Amnesio is a small, blue beetle/cicada-like experiment with a round body, two thick arms, two thick legs, a purple mark on his stomach, two large wings on his back with purple spots on them, a round face with large black eyes, a little mouth, and two thin antennae. ===Powers and abilities=== Amnesio can produce a red laser vision from his eyes that erases the memories of anyone hit in the eyes. If he hears the password "''[[Pelekai ʻohana|ʻohana]]''" (which means "family" in [[Hawaii]]an), his eyes will flash red and the memories of all his victims will be restored. In the ''[[Stitch!]]'' anime, it is revealed that Amnesio stores his victims' memories in pouches under his wings. If his victims ingest the pouch with their memories in it, their memories will be fully restored. ==Appearances== ===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''=== Experiment 303 was the 303rd genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Dr. Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to wipe individuals' memories. 303 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch|Experiment 626]]. All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of Kauai. 303's pod was used as a ping-pong ball by [[Keoni Jameson|Keoni]] and another player until it got whacked off the table and into a little boy's bucket of sand. Thinking the pod was a marble, the boy put it on top of his sand castle. A small wave then splashed over the castle, activating 303, which caused the boy to flee [[Lahui Beach|the beach]] in terror. 303 then proceeded to erase individuals' memories, including a married couple whose wife clashed with her husband after losing her memory. Meanwhile, [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]] and [[Stitch]] handed out homemade invitations to the former's birthday party. Later, [[Captain Gantu|Gantu]] tracked 303 down but found it quite difficult to subdue the latter while he was airborne, as he managed to successfully evade all of Gantu's plasma blasts. Gantu and 303's presence caught the attention of Lilo and Stitch. Grabbing a butterfly net, Stitch climbed a telephone pole to try to ensnare 303 as the latter perched on a power line, but he was instead captured in a [[Prison Capsule|containment orb]] by Gantu. Lilo, Stitch, and Gantu were soon fighting over the captive experiment, which shortly ended with 303 wiping all three of their memories, leaving the trio dazed. Plagued with amnesia, Lilo and Gantu decided to team up and figure out what to do with the captured experiment. Stitch, however, reverted to his original programming, while Lilo and Gantu assumed he was an escaped convict. With their memories erased, Lilo and Gantu (dubbed Martha and Lenny) went after Stitch and also did recreational activities together at some point. They later ran into [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] and [[Pleakley]], where 303 wiped both of their memories as well, but not before they explained to Lilo, Stitch, and Gantu exactly who was on whose team. Lilo and Stitch then decided to team up to get their memories back. Gantu wanted to come along too, but Lilo was unsure of him after learning that he was actually an evil experiment hunter. After Lilo and Stitch discovered how to reverse 303's amnesia effects via [[Jumba's Computer|Jumba's computer]], a dismayed Gantu set the experiment free. Lilo grew devastated, even though Gantu stated that he didn't want his memory back. Fortunately, Stitch was able to use his binocular vision to locate 303, and the trio chased him into a factory. Despite Gantu's protests, Lilo undid 303's effects by shouting out, "''[[Pelekai ʻohana|ʻOhana]]''!" Although everyone got their memories back, Gantu managed to recapture 303 after a long pursuit and take off with him. 303, named Amnesio, was successfully sent to an impatient [[Dr. Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]], where the former ended up erasing Hämsterviel's memory also. Gantu falsely described him as a dangerous criminal named "Doofus" who had just been captured by Ace Jackson (Gantu) while admiring a pottery jar that read "World's Greatest Cop", which Lilo had made Gantu sometime earlier. In "[[Woops (episode)|Woops]]", Amnesio was sent back to Gantu along with all of Hämsterviel's other captive experiments after [[Woops|Experiment 600]] caused chaos and nearly blew Hämsterviel's cover to the [[UGF Troopers|prison guards]]. Amnesio reappeared in "[[Snafu (episode)|Snafu]]", and was freed along with Gantu's other captive experiments by Lilo, Stitch, and several other experiments in a rescue mission. ===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''=== In the film's opening, Amnesio can be seen waving hello to [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]], along with [[Snooty]] and [[Babyfier]]. Later, the first 624 experiments, including Amnesio, were rounded up by [[Leroy]] and taken to a stadium to be destroyed. However, Lilo, [[Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben]], and [[Captain Gantu|Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed. Amnesio participated in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]] by erasing Leroys' memories. However, the Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle, but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben, and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe. ===''[[Stitch!]]''=== Amnesio made an appearance in the ''Stitch!'' anime where he used his powers on [[BooGoo]], [[Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Captain Gantu|Gantu]], [[Reuben]], and [[Dr. Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]. It is revealed that Amnesio holds the stored memories in pouches under his wings. If his victims ingest the pouch with their memories in it, everyone's memory will be fully restored. Only Amnesio knows whose pouch belongs to whom. Also, it is shown that when Amnesio's powers are used on Stitch, he reverts to his original programming since he is nothing but instinct in that state. ==Gallery== {{Gallerylink}} ==Trivia== *Amnesio was first revealed in a DVD bonus feature of ''[[Stitch! The Movie]]'' in the experiment gallery. *His name is a pun on "amnesia", which refers to memory loss. *Amnesio, [[Bugby]], [[Babyfier]], [[Jam]], [[Melty]], [[Wishy-Washy]], [[Snooty]], [[Hunkahunka]], [[Experiments#5-Series: Elemental and environmental manipulators|Blake]], [[Slugger]], [[Witch (Lilo & Stitch)|Witch]], and two [[Unconfirmed Experiments#Comic Zone Volume 1: Disney's Lilo & Stitch|unconfirmed]] [[Unconfirmed Experiments#Miscellaneous|experiments]] are the only known experiments that have wings. *Amnesio is one of the few known experiments whose powers Stitch is vulnerable to. **He is also one of the few known experiments whose powers Lilo falls victim to. *Amnesio is not referred to by his new name at any point in [[Amnesio (episode)|his debut]], but his name officially appears on the experiments list in the end credits of ''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''. *In his episode, when Amnesio flies around in several instances, the song "{{WikipediaLink|Flight of the Bumblebee}}" is heard playing. *The password which reverses Amnesio's mind-erasing effects is "''[[Pelekai ʻohana|ʻohana]]''", a [[Hawaii]]an word that Jumba did not know of until well after Amnesio's creation. **According to [[Jess Winfield]], "Jumba obviously changed the password for Amnesio after arrival on Earth, when he learned about ''ʻohana''." Because "it's always wise to change your passwords occasionally!"{{cite web|url=http://lasfansite.atspace.me/stuff/history/tvtome/page04.html|title=L&S Says Mahalo|website=[[wikipedia:TV.com|TV Tome]]|date=December 14, 2004|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20160305082355/http://lasfansite.atspace.me/stuff/history/tvtome/page04.html|archivedate=March 19, 2016|accessdate=May 27, 2018}} *Amnesio is the first experiment to be caught by Gantu onscreen; Gantu had previously caught a "[[Nosox|sock hider]]" and "[[Experiments#3-Series: Psychological|pudding stealer]]". *Amnesio's [[Experiment Pods|pod]] color is yellow. *The [[Experiment Pod Container]] describes Amnesio as: "Experiment 303. Primary function: Erases memories." **It seems that Amnesio specifically erases memories of personal identity and relationships with others; victims still retain other learned behaviors, such as language and societal norms. *Amnesio is one of the few experiments to not have his one true place revealed. *Amnesio's head appears in the online game ''[[Jumba's Lab]]''. ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== *{{L&S|Amnesio (303)}} {{Lilo & Stitch}} [[Category:Lilo & Stitch characters]] [[Category:Lilo & Stitch Experiments]] [[Category:Males]] [[Category:Creatures]] [[Category:Aliens]] [[Category:Disney characters]] [[Category:Bugs]] [[Category:Animated characters]] [[Category:Silent characters]] [[Category:Stitch! characters]]

[[Experiments]] ("cousins")}} '''Morpholomew''', also known as '''Experiment 316''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. He is designed to morph organisms into an exact duplicate of any other, after seeing the target organism or a photo of it for reference; however, the recipient's vocal cords will stay identical. His one true place is at a costume store, morphing people into celebrities. ==Background== ===Personality=== Morpholomew is very curious, as seen when he chased a noise which turned out to be a rabbit. He is also one of the few experiments that demand payment, which he considers to be chicken legs. He enjoys chicken legs so much that he can easily go through several buckets of them in only a few minutes. While he is cautious of others at first, he is friendly and trusting, as he immediately befriended [[Stitch]] after the latter pursued him and pronounced him his cousin and ally, even shaking hands. He is fairly relaxed and doesn't mind helping individuals. He also seems to have a sense of humor, as he once changed [[Captain Gantu|Gantu]] into a harmless bunny. ===Physical appearance=== Morpholomew is a small, red blob-like experiment with a small body, two small arms, two short legs, a short tail, a thin mouth, and black eyes. ===Powers and abilities=== Morpholomew can alter the appearance of any organism into any other organism, even if it is not the same species. To do this, he must see the target organism or a photo of the target at least once before he can change them. He then touches the recipient while briefly changing his own head to that of the target organism and morphs their appearance to that of the target's. The recipient's vocal cords stay identical, however. ==Appearances== ===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''=== Experiment 316 was the 316th genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Dr. Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to morph organisms into any other organism. 316 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch|Experiment 626]]. All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of Kauai, with 316's pod landing on a hay umbrella. At the very beginning of the [[Morpholomew (episode)|episode]], [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]] decided to enter the local skateboarding competition in order to win a brand-new skateboard, the Velociraptor 1200, for her crush [[Keoni Jameson|Keoni]]. Before the event, she and [[Stitch]] discovered Experiment 316, whose pod was activated in a fountain after Stitch unstuck Lilo's skateboard from a straw umbrella. According to [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], Experiment 316, or Morpholomew, was a creature capable of giving anyone the appearance of someone else. Lilo used this power in order to enter the competition as Keoni. In the meantime, [[Jake Long|Jake]], [[Luong Lao Shi|Lao Shi]], [[Fu Dog]], [[Trixie Carter|Trixie]], and [[Arthur Spudinski|Spud]] arrived at the Kauai skate park. They were investigating reports of undisguised magical creatures lurking on the island of [[Hawaii]] (actually Jumba's illegal genetic experiments), although Jake was more interested in winning the contest's grand prize. All of them separated to go on their own business: Lao Shi became enamored with [[Mrs. Hasagawa]]; Trixie and Spud headed to the beach; Fu Dog went to place some bets on Jake while the latter signed up for the skateboarding competition. Lilo did the same, but soon realized that impersonating Keoni was likely a bad idea when she earned a low score. She asked Morpholomew to change her into absolutely anybody else so she could start over, but registrations closed before she got a chance to sign up again. Elsewhere, Jake, having spotted Morpholomew with Lilo and mistaking the little red blob for a magical creature, transformed into the American Dragon and got ready to pursue them. However, he was [[Prison Capsule|captured]] by [[Captain Gantu|Gantu]], who mistook him for Morpholomew. Since Jake didn't show for the competition, Lilo decided to ask Morpholomew to turn her into Jake so she could enter in his stead. Meanwhile, Jake managed to escape [[Gantu's Ship|Gantu's ship]] before he was transferred to [[Dr. Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s [[Prison Asteroid K-37|asteroid]] and went back to the skate park. However, Lilo had already taken his place and failed once again to score any points. Trixie and Spud grew suspicious of Lilo (still disguised as Jake) while she threw a tantrum when Stitch told her that Morpholomew (who earlier got distracted by a rabbit) had been captured by Gantu. They knew something was up when Lilo panicked upon hearing Fu Dog speak. The real Jake (in his [[Dragons (Jake Long Universe)|dragon]] form) arrived at that moment and engaged in a duel with Stitch. Before things got too far, Lilo managed to calm everyone down and explain the whole situation. Once everything was clarified, everyone decided to team up to retrieve Morpholomew. They traveled over to Gantu's ship and fought against him for Morpholomew. In the confusion, Jake and company tricked Gantu into thinking he captured Morpholomew, when in reality, Spud assumed the little red blob's form and got kidnapped instead. Thanks to this, the team managed to get Morpholomew back and change Gantu into a little white bunny as punishment for all the trouble he caused. The gang then headed back to the skateboard competition, where the winner claimed the Velociraptor 1200. Jake and Lilo were a bit bummed out by this, but were happy to have made new friends. They left on good terms and promised to see each other again soon. Meanwhile, Morpholomew was given a one true place at a costume store, where he morphed people into celebrities according to the photo he was shown. ===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''=== Morpholomew was seen early in the movie morphing the [[Ice Cream Man]] into the famous [[Elvis Presley|Elvis]] as [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]] was making her rounds with [[Scrump]] to make sure all the experiments were happy in the one true place they belonged. Later, the first 624 experiments, including Morpholomew, were rounded up by [[Leroy]] and taken to a stadium to be destroyed. However, Lilo, [[Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben]], and [[Captain Gantu|Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed. It is unknown whether or not Morpholomew participated in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]]. The Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben, and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe. ===''[[Stitch!]]''=== Morpholomew made an appearance in the ''[[Stitch!]]'' anime where [[Dr. Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]] transmutated him to morph his own body instead of others and also gave him a vocabulary. Ani met Stitch, who mistook her for a de-aged Lilo, and they played together contentedly. Hämsterviel took advantage of this and sent [[Captain Gantu|Gantu]] to use Morpholomew to take the image of her and distract Stitch long enough to capture him. Morpholomew later appeared as one of the experiments who helped Stitch fight [[Dark End]]. Silliness inducement |paraphernalia = Spines |status = Active |creator = [[Jumba Jookiba]] |family = [[Experiments]] ("cousins")}} '''Spike''', also known as '''Experiment 319''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. He is designed to alter the intelligence of entire populations by shooting quills that increase their silliness by 99% when struck, leaving them only 1% clever for the next 48 hours. His one true place is in [[Pleakley]]'s E.A.R.W.A.X. group, hugging and thus taming other truant experiments, after he is given protective armor to cover his goofiness-inducing spines. ==Background== ===Personality=== Spike is shown to be troublesome, as his spines pose a dangerous threat to anyone pricked by them. He also has a feisty side to him and will attack any target, even if he is outnumbered. However, he is not afraid to express emotion as shown when he tearfully cried his heart out while Pleakley hugged him during the E.A.R.W.A.X. session. This not only rehabilitated Spike, but also motivated him to be a hugging therapist and follow Pleakley's hugging-and-crying method. ===Physical appearance=== Spike is a large, quadrupedal, dark blue pangolin/porcupine-like experiment covered in incredibly sharp white-tipped spines from his head down to his long tail. He has black eyes, a red nose, and sharp black claws. His face, underbelly, and paws are white, and the only areas not covered in spines. ===Powers and abilities=== Spike can fire his spines like darts that are capable of hitting multiple targets at once. His quills also contain a venom that increases the victim's goofiness by 99% when struck, leaving them only 1% clever. His quills can poke and affect anyone, even if Spike had no intention when he is being friendly. In the ''[[Stitch!]]'' anime, it is also revealed that Spike can roll into a ball and launch his spikes while spinning at incredibly high speeds after being transmutated by [[Dr. Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]. ===Weaknesses=== The effect of Spike's spines wears off within 48 hours. Also, he is emotionally susceptible to hugging therapy. ==Appearances== ===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''=== Experiment 319 was the 319th genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Dr. Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to fire spines like darts that make his victims unintelligent by causing any hit victim's goofiness level to increase by 99%, leaving them only 1% clever. 319 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch|Experiment 626]]. All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of Kauai, with 319's pod landing by an outdoor stage. When a clumsy servant carrying drinking water bumped into [[Dr. Gladys Okra|the public speaker]], the water bottle on the tray fell onto the stage and trickled out, which touched 319's pod, activating the experiment. 319 then climbed onto the stage and spiked Dr. Okra and her servant, causing them to act goofy. He next rolled in front of the entire audience and attacked them as well, scaring them all away. Later, 319 attacked a museum until he was captured in a [[Prison Capsule|containment orb]] by [[Stitch]], but not before spiking him and [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]]. Luckily, 319's goofiness-inducing spines didn't seem to affect Jumba as much as Stitch (since the former was already a genius). 319 was then taken back to the [[Lilo's House|Pelekai residence]] and named Spike, who ultimately served as one of the experiments in [[Pleakley]]'s E.A.R.W.A.X. group. While the captive Spike was being rehabilitated, [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]] made a vain attempt to get a goofy Stitch to become smart again in time for the upcoming Ohana-Rama. During Pleakley's seminar, he bored most of the experiments while discussing therapy topics from Dr. Okra. When a fight broke out between [[Slushy]] and [[Splodyhead]], a stray fireball from Splodyhead destroyed Spike's container, freeing him. Spike then went on a rampage, chasing [[Nosy]] around the house and eventually targeting Pleakley. Forced to resolve the issue, Pleakley left for a moment, rummaged through the closet, and donned makeshift armor against Spike's spines. He then attempted hugging therapy on Spike, which surprisingly pacified the latter who sobbed pitifully. The other experiments, awed by Spike's outcome, tried out Pleakley's hugging-and-crying method as well. The following night, Lilo, Stitch, Jumba, Pleakley, and Spike attended the Ohana-Rama, where [[Mertle Edmonds|Mertle]] sunk Lilo's team by answering each question correctly. Spike then offered Lilo a hug to cheer her up when she felt discouraged. She declined, however, because although Spike was rehabilitated, a stray spine would likely affect her intelligence. Later during the quiz contest, Lilo and Spike followed Stitch backstage (when he ran after an [[Elvis Presley|Elvis]] CD he unstuck from his nose) to discover that [[Elena, Teresa, and Yuki|Teresa]] was secretly helping Mertle cheat. Thus, Lilo convinced Spike to hug Teresa, who got pricked and kept giving Mertle completely silly answers as a result. After Lilo won the Ohana-Rama, Mertle stormed out in a rage. Spike felt sorry for Mertle and decided to hug her as well, spiking the latter. Spike later found his one true place in Pleakley's E.A.R.W.A.X. group, where he used hugging therapy to tame other truant experiments while wearing similar protective armor to cover his goofiness-inducing spines, with Nosy even becoming one of Spike's patients. ===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''=== The first 624 experiments, including Spike, were rounded up by [[Leroy]] and taken to a stadium to be destroyed. However, [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]], [[Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben]], and [[Captain Gantu|Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed. Spike participated in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]] by firing goofiness-inducing spines at attacking Leroys. However, the Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle, but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben, and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe. ===''[[Stitch!]]''=== Spike has appeared multiple times in the ''Stitch!'' anime, including one instance in Season 2, along with [[Hammerface]], [[Babyfier]], [[Link]], and [[Woody (Lilo & Stitch)|Woody]]. It is revealed that [[Dr. Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]] reverted these experiments to evil using a recording of [[Angel (Lilo & Stitch)|Angel]]'s song, thus enabling them to wreak havoc on the [[Izayoi Island|island]]. In another episode, Spike was also used by Hämsterviel to try to sabotage a quiz competition. His abilities were modified in this episode so that he only reduces the victim's intelligence, and it can be magnified by squeezing his nose. It is also shown that he has the ability to roll into a ball and launch his spikes while spinning at incredibly high speeds. In "Shogun", it is shown that Spike was dehydrated back into an experiment pod and locked in [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]]'s vault. Spike later appeared as one of the experiments who helped [[Stitch]] fight [[Dark End]]. He also appeared in the special ''Stitch and the Planet of Sand''. ==Gallery== {{Gallerylink}} ==Trivia== *Spike is clearly based on porcupines, but unlike him, real-life porcupines cannot throw/shoot their quills, nor are their spines poisonous. *When Jumba got pricked by Spike, he did not appear to be affected. However, he states that he is not immune to the effects of his creation, and that he does not act silly because even 1% of his intelligence is far superior to that of an average human being's intelligence. *Spike is one of the few known experiments whose powers Stitch is vulnerable to. *Spike, along with [[Gigi]], [[Dorkifier]], [[Nosox]], [[Experiments#2-Series: Technological and scientific|Butter]], [[Shortstuff]], [[Yang]], [[Richter]], [[Phoon]], [[Tank (Lilo & Stitch)|Tank]], [[Splodyhead]], and one [[Unconfirmed Experiments#Leroy & Stitch|unconfirmed experiment]], are the only known experiments that are primarily quadrupeds. *Spike is one of the six known experiments to be rehabilitated by someone other than Lilo and Stitch, the other five being Gigi, [[Elastico]], [[Yaarp]], [[Frenchfry]], and [[Snooty]]. **Spike, alongside Yaarp, was rehabilitated by Pleakley. *Spike's [[Experiment Pods|pod]] color is yellow in [[Lilo & Stitch: The Series|the original series]]. In the ''[[Stitch!]]'' anime, it is white. *In the English dub of the anime episode "Link-age", [[Reuben]] states that Spike's favorite type of sandwich is a {{WikipediaLink|shish kebab}} {{WikipediaLink|Gyros|gyro}}. ==External links== *{{L&S|Spike (319)|Spike}} {{Lilo & Stitch}} {{DISPLAYTITLE:Spike}} [[es:Spike (Lilo & Stitch)]] [[fr:Spike (Lilo & Stitch)]] [[Category:Lilo & Stitch characters]] [[Category:Lilo & Stitch Experiments]] [[Category:Aliens]] [[Category:Monsters]] [[Category:Males]] [[Category:Creatures]] [[Category:Disney characters]] [[Category:Silent characters]] [[Category:Stitch! characters]]

[[Experiments]] ("cousins")}} '''Heckler''', also known as '''Experiment 322''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. He is designed to undermine enemy morale with verbal abuse. His one true place is in a dunk tank, provoking people to try and dunk him. ==Background== ===Personality=== Although Heckler acts like a jerk most of the time, he really just seems to insult out of impulse. He cannot help but make fun of others, but has been proven to be willing to help people, especially when it comes to insult comedy. Most of the time, he does not entirely intend to offend others, but it is in his programming, and he cannot help but throw around a few insults. If not, he breaks down into a fit of self-pity, as he has never had any other purpose. He proved to be so annoying that even [[Dr. Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]], who usually wanted all of [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]]'s experiments, didn't want him. Heckler has the ability to be kind-hearted, but just has a very strange way of showing it. He loves his job being in the dunk tank and encouraging people to try to dunk him for charity, smiling good-naturedly right before Mertle dunked him. When he insults someone, it can be hard to tell if it is out of reflex, just teasing, or actually trying to be hurtful. ===Physical appearance=== Heckler is an orange experiment that resembles a cross between [[Reuben|625]] and [[627]], with short pointed ears, small beady eyes, an oval nose, a wide mouth with large fangs, and a shirt and bow tie imprint on his body. His head also has markings that resemble a balding head, with hair on the sides, much like [[Don Rickles]]' hair as he got older. ===Powers and abilities=== As his name suggests, Heckler is a master heckler who can use verbal insults towards others to even defend himself against enemies. He can speak fluently and is capable of making jokes about individuals' appearances and/or personalities. Heckler appears to be very agile, as he was able to easily flee from [[Captain Gantu|Gantu]] while being chased. He also seems to be super strong, as he was able to wrestle [[Stitch]]. ==Appearances== ===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''=== Experiment 322 was the 322nd genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Dr. Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to crush his victims' pride and self-confidence with verbal insults. 322 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch|Experiment 626]]. All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of Kauai. Experiment 322 was activated off-screen at the [[Birds of Paradise Hotel]], where he managed to impress a crowd of tourists by insulting the tour guide's hair and shirt, earning 322 a round of applause from the crowd. 322 was later chased around [[Kokaua Town|town]] by [[Gantu]], but the former was able to stay ahead by repeatedly insulting Gantu until 322 was soon rescued by [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]] and [[Stitch]]. When 322 antagonized Stitch, the latter attempted to beat him up, only to be stopped by Lilo, who considered 322 to be somewhat useful. Lilo then brought 322, whom she named Heckler, to [[Mertle's House|Mertle's house]] as revenge, where Heckler insulted [[Mertle Edmonds|Mertle]]'s hair and glasses, much to Lilo and Stitch's humor. Lilo and Stitch shortly after took Heckler back to their [[Lilo's House|house]], where he insulted their dwelling and later both [[Nani Pelekai|Nani]] and [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]]. When Jumba tried to silence Heckler by stuffing Stitch into his mouth, the latter spat Stitch out and insulted how he tasted, which led to them tussling on the floor. Nani rejected Heckler's presence and requested Lilo to keep him out of sight until after the charity event that Nani was hosting. Later, Lilo and Stitch looked to Heckler for guidance for [[Pleakley]]'s stand-up comedy at Nani's charity event, and Heckler convinced them to give the audience rotten tomatoes to throw at Pleakley's rotten jokes. Although uncertain, Lilo and Stitch took Heckler's advice (unaware that he was leading them astray). At Nani's charity event, Heckler's insults towards the staff caused all of them to quit. When Nani then demanded Lilo to get rid of Heckler, the latter insulted Lilo's voice and nose before attempting to escape. Gantu then barged in for Heckler, but since Nani, Lilo, and Stitch were sick of Heckler's verbal abuse, they gladly handed him over. Gantu took Heckler back to [[Gantu's Ship|his ship]], where he prepared to transport the latter to [[Dr. Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]. However, Heckler's insults towards Hämsterviel ultimately prompted him to order Gantu to release Heckler. Thus, Heckler returned to Nani's charity event, where he was soon chased by Stitch. While being pursued, Heckler caused massive chaos at the dining tables by kicking and throwing food at people, including Nani. Heckler then threw a rotten tomato at one of Pleakley's bad jokes and went onstage to insult him in front of everyone. At that moment, however, Pleakley and Lilo (as well as the entire audience) accepted that Heckler's insults towards them were true, leaving him defeated and sobbing on the stage. After Lilo managed to console Heckler, she found his one true place in a dunk tank, where he provoked people to try and dunk him, especially a vengeful Mertle. ===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''=== The first 624 experiments, including Heckler, were rounded up by [[Leroy]] and taken to a stadium to be destroyed. However, [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]], [[Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben]], and [[Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed. Heckler participated in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]], but it is unknown what he did. The Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle, but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben, and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe. ==Gallery== {{Gallerylink}} ==Trivia== *Heckler was possibly inspired by [[Don Rickles]], a comedian who was known for insulting people for humorous effect. *According to Jumba, Heckler was programmed "to destroy enemy's confidence by mercilessly taunting and humiliating him," and is one of the best ideas he ever had. *Heckler was activated off-screen. *Heckler is one of the few known experiments that can speak fluently. *The [[Experiment Pod Container]] describes Heckler as: "Experiment 322. Primary function: Undermine enemy morale with verbal abuse." *Oddly, when Heckler's image is reflected off of Stitch's eyes in ''[[The Origin of Stitch]]'', he is gagged and handcuffed for some reason. *Heckler is one of the few experiments to not appear in the group photo at the end of ''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''. *If it weren't for Hamsterviel ordering Gantu to free Heckler, the latter would've been the sixth experiment that Lilo and Stitch willingly handed Gantu to. **Piggybacking on that, Heckler returning to Lilo and Stitch was likely karma for all the times they let Gantu take some of the experiments. ==External links== *{{L&S|Heckler (322)}} {{Lilo & Stitch}} [[Category:Males]] [[Category:Lilo & Stitch Experiments]] [[Category:Lilo & Stitch characters]] [[Category:Aliens]] [[Category:Creatures]] [[Category:Disney characters]] [[Category:Animated characters]]
