[[Experiments]] ("cousins")}} '''Hunkahunka''', also known as '''Experiment 323''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. He is designed to cause societies to come to a crashing standstill by causing artificial lovesickness. Once he pecks someone, they fall in love with the first individual they see regardless of their gender, species, and personal preferences; only spraying water in the victim's face will break the spell. He was captured by [[Gantu]], but was rescued in "[[Snafu (episode)|Snafu]]". ==Background== ===Physical appearance=== Hunkahunka is a small pink/purple hummingbird-like experiment with a large head, black eyes, dark pink and maroon feathers on his body, a long lavender beak, light pink belly and purple-tipped wings and tail. ===Powers and abilities=== Hunkahunka can peck a target which injects the victim with a love-inducing drug that affects certain nerves, causing an artificial "love" sensation in which they are attracted to the first individual they see, regardless of the individual's gender, species, and personal preferences. ==Appearances== ===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''=== Experiment 323 was the 323rd genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Dr. Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel's]] funding. He was designed to use his fake love-inducing ability to bring entire civilizations to a lovestruck standstill. 323 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch|Experiment 626]]. All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of Kauai. At an unknown point, Experiment 323 was activated off-screen (possibly by an ocean wave). 323 then proceeded to cause artificial love across the island. He first targeted [[David Kawena|David]] and pecked the latter to make him fall for some other woman on [[Lahui Beach|the beach]], making [[Nani Pelekai|Nani]] jealous after she agreed to go on a date with David. Later, [[Captain Gantu|Gantu]] attempted to capture 323 after noticing the experiment, but was thwarted by [[Stitch]]. When Gantu restrained Stitch and prepared to shoot the latter into the ocean (knowing he would drown), 323 pecked Gantu to make him fall in love with [[Pleakley]]. Stitch freed himself and managed to capture 323 in a drink cooler. He then showed 323, named Hunkahunka, to [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]], who used the experiment's fake love-inducing power to make [[Keoni Jameson|Keoni]] fall for her. However, Hunkahunka escaped and resumed his love-inflicting rampage while being pursued by Stitch and Gantu. At one point, he pecked Gantu again, causing the latter to temporarily fall for Stitch. While Stitch evaded Gantu, the former was able to recapture Hunkahunka and hide him in a raffle box. When Lilo ran into Stitch, fed up with Keoni's phony love, she attempted to grab the raffle box from him (thinking it contained the antidote), causing the box to open and Hunkahunka to get loose again. Later on, Hunkahunka entered a dance hall, where he caused countless victims to fall in love, and pecked Nani at one point to make her fall for Gantu. Eventually, after a long chase, Gantu managed to capture Hunkahunka in a [[Prison Capsule|containment orb]] and take off with him. Regardless, Lilo ultimately decided that people should want others to love them for who they are, not merely because some alien bird pecked them. Hunkahunka was successfully sent to an impatient [[Dr. Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]], where the former then pecked Hämsterviel, causing him to fall for Gantu, much to the latter's surprise. However, he still berated Gantu like he would on a regular basis, implying that either Hunkahunka's love powers had a somewhat different effect on Hämsterviel, or he has a different point of view altogether. Although Hunkahunka was unseen in "[[Woops (episode)|Woops]]", he is known to have been sent back to Gantu along with all of Hämsterviel's other captive experiments after [[Woops|Experiment 600]] caused chaos and nearly blew Hämsterviel's cover to the [[UGF Troopers|prison guards]]. Hunkahunka reappeared in "[[Snafu (episode)|Snafu]]", and was freed along with Gantu's other captive experiments by Lilo, Stitch, and several other experiments in a rescue mission. ===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''=== The first 624 experiments, including Hunkahunka, were rounded up by [[Leroy]] and taken to a stadium to be destroyed. However, [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]], [[Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben]], and [[Captain Gantu|Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed. Hunkahunka participated in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]], as he was seen among the other experiments. The Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle, but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben, and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe. ===''[[Stitch!]]''=== Hunkahunka made an appearance in the ''Stitch!'' anime where [[Stitch]] used him on [[Angel (Lilo & Stitch)|Angel]] after she got mad at him earlier. However, Hunkahunka's spell caused Angel to become overly obsessed with Stitch, therefore teaching him a lesson when Hunkahunka also made others fall in love (including [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], who was about to reveal the antidote before becoming part of Hunkahunka's spell). ==Gallery== {{Gallerylink}} ==Trivia== *Hunkahunka was first revealed in a DVD bonus feature of ''[[Stitch! The Movie]]'' in the experiment gallery. *Hunkahunka is based on {{WikipediaLink|Cupid}}. *Hunkahunka is named after a lyric in the [[Elvis Presley]] song "[[Burning Love]]", played in [[Lilo & Stitch|the original movie]]. Lilo refers to him as a "Hunkahunka bird of love". *Hunkahunka, [[Bugby]], [[Babyfier]], [[Jam]], [[Melty]], [[Wishy-Washy]], [[Snooty]], [[Amnesio]], [[Experiments#5-Series: Elemental and environmental manipulators|Blake]], [[Slugger]], [[Witch (Lilo & Stitch)|Witch]], and two [[Unconfirmed Experiments#Comic Zone Volume 1: Disney's Lilo & Stitch|unconfirmed]] [[Unconfirmed Experiments#Miscellaneous|experiments]] are the only known experiments that have wings. *Hunkahunka was activated off-screen. *In [[Hunkahunka (episode)|his debut]], Hunkahunka had dark purple feathers. However, in official media, [[Aloha, E Komo Mai|the show's intro]], the episode "[[Snafu (episode)|Snafu]]", and his later appearances, he had dark pink and maroon feathers on his body. ==External links== *{{L&S|Hunkahunka (323)}} {{Lilo & Stitch}} [[Category:Lilo & Stitch characters]] [[Category:Aliens]] [[Category:Birds]] [[Category:Lilo & Stitch Experiments]] [[Category:Males]] [[Category:Animated characters]] [[Category:Silent characters]] [[Category:Disney characters]] [[Category:Stitch! characters]]

Clone generator |home = [[Hawaii]] |likes = Generating clones |dislikes = Weak clones, being captured |powers = Duplication |status = Active |creator = [[Jumba Jookiba]] |family = [[Experiments]] ("cousins")}} '''Dupe''', also known as '''Experiment 344''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. He is designed to generate infinite clones of individuals, but his programming is considered a failure because the original's power is distributed evenly among the duplicates, resulting in them being inferior in everything. Luckily, it is possible for him to reverse the cloning. His one true place is making half-calorie [[Luki's Shave Ice|shave ice]] cones with [[Slushy]]. ==Background== ===Personality=== Dupe is shown to be very fun-loving, childish, and immature, due to the fact that he was programmed to be one of the younger experiments (along with [[Mr. Stenchy]] and [[Babyfier]]). Because of this, he is often treated as the baby of the heroes' side, as his cloning powers are neither chaotic nor destructive. He is also playful, friendly, and optimistic. ===Physical appearance=== Dupe is a small, golden-yellow experiment resembling a cross between a monkey, lemur, and raccoon. He has relatively flat ears, a brown round nose, black eyes, a white body, a brown-striped, raccoon-like tail, and brown-striped prehensile appendage protruding from his head. ===Powers and abilities=== The ray from Dupe's appendage can cause any individual or object hit to split into a varying number of duplicates. However, any traits (such as strength, power, calories, etc.) would be divided between the duplicates making the original very weak, and resulting in the original and duplicates being inferior in everything. His ray can also be used to remerge the clones into the original. In the ''[[Stitch!]]'' anime, Dupe was altered by [[Dr. Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]], so instead of making things weaker once duplicated, the clones were made stronger than the original, with each newly-created duplicate being slightly bigger and stronger than the one created before it, while the original maintained its normal strength. However, his tweak had a downside in which the enhanced replicas had a significantly reduced shelf life and disappeared after about an hour. ==Appearances== ===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''=== Experiment 344 was the 344th genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Dr. Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to clone single individuals into entire armies and make infinite weapons, but all of the original's traits were divided between them and the clones. 344 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch|Experiment 626]]. All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of Kauai. At an unknown point after this, Experiment 344 was activated. An estimated twelve hours after his activation, 344 was [[Prison Capsule|captured]] by [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]] and [[Stitch]] and taken back to their [[Lilo's House|house]], but not before being pursued by a relentless [[Captain Gantu|Gantu]]. After [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] explained about 344's powers, the latter demonstrated by duplicating a lollipop and birthday cake (with less calories in each). Stitch then attempted to use 344 to clone [[Pleakley]] as well, despite the latter's protests. Fortunately, Jumba put 344 away on [[Jumba's Ship|his ship]] to prevent any further chaos. The following night, after [[Mertle Edmonds|Mertle]] and [[Elena, Teresa, and Yuki|the hula girls]] did not show up at Lilo's slumber party that she had hosted earlier, Lilo used 344, christened Dupe, to generate clones of herself that she could befriend. However, Stitch hastily intervened, resulting in him being cloned into three instead. Later that night, Gantu, [[Hammerface|033]], [[Heat|609]], [[Thresher|544]], and [[Plasmoid|617]] attacked the Pelekai residence. Stitch and his clones tried to fight back, but due to a side effect from Dupe's replication, they had all become very weak, enabling Gantu and his four henchmen experiments to easily defeat and capture Stitch and his duplicates in containment orbs. Shortly after Stitch had been kidnapped, Lilo hatched a plan and used Dupe to generate three clones of Pleakley, leaving the original comatose. Lilo and the Pleakley clones then launched a rescue mission on [[Gantu's Ship|Gantu's ship]] while taking Dupe with them so he could remerge the Stitch clones. Gantu complained about the victory feast that [[Reuben|Experiment 625]] made for him and his minions, when he was distracted by Lilo and the Pleakley clones on his ship. After Gantu discovered them and Lilo informed him about Dupe's cloning powers, Gantu grabbed Dupe and cloned Hammerface, Heat, Thresher, and Plasmoid each into a hundred replicas. However, as a result of being tricked, the experiments had all become complete weaklings, and thus were easily defeated by Lilo and the Pleakleys. Lilo then used Dupe to remerge the freed Stitch clones into the original, and Lilo, Stitch, Dupe, and the Pleakley clones escaped the ship. Dupe then remerged the Pleakley clones into the original, and he was later found a one true place making half-calorie [[Luki's Shave Ice|shave ice]]. In "[[Remmy (episode)|Remmy]]", Dupe was one of the experiments in Lilo's dream. In "[[Snafu (episode)|Snafu]]", Dupe and [[Slushy]] were seen using their combined powers to sell multiple low-calorie shave ice cones that [[Charles and Mary|a couple]] bought and enjoyed. Gantu then attempted to revert the rehabilitated experiments to evil by playing a recording of [[Angel (Lilo & Stitch)|Angel]]'s song with Reuben's help, but due to interference from [[Snafu|Experiment 120]], Gantu's karaoke tape was played instead, much to Slushy and Dupe's humor. ===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''=== The first 624 experiments, including Dupe, were rounded up by [[Leroy]] and taken to a stadium to be destroyed. However, [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]], [[Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben]], and [[Captain Gantu|Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed. Dupe participated in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]] by splitting attacking Leroys into weakling Leroys. However, the Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben, and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe. ===''[[Stitch!]]''=== Dupe made an appearance in the ''Stitch!'' anime where his tweak was altered by [[Dr. Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]], so instead of making things weaker once duplicated, the clones are made stronger (and bigger) than the original. ==Gallery== {{Gallerylink}} ==Trivia== *According to Jumba, Dupe "is [a] duplicator. It can make multiple copies of anyone or anything. Designed to make infinite number of weapons." However, Dupe "was [a] failure. Duplicates were not as powerful as [the] original." *Dupe is one of the few known experiments whose powers Stitch is vulnerable to. *Dupe was activated off-screen. *The [[Hammerface]], [[Heat]], [[Thresher]], and [[Plasmoid]] clones were never remerged into the originals by Dupe, but each of these experiments appeared as one again in later episodes. It is presumed that [[Dr. Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]] was somehow able to remerge these clones into the originals, meaning that there are ways to reverse the cloning without Dupe. *Dupe's antenna and ears appear in the online game ''[[Jumba's Lab]]''. *Dupe also appears in the online game ''[[Lilo & Stitch: Alien Interception]]'' along with Plasmoid, [[Tank (Lilo & Stitch)|Tank]], [[Clyde (Lilo & Stitch)|Clyde]], [[Yang]], and Hämsterviel. ==External links== *{{L&S|Dupe (344)}} {{Lilo & Stitch}} [[Category:Lilo & Stitch characters]] [[Category:Lilo & Stitch Experiments]] [[Category:Aliens]] [[Category:Monsters]] [[Category:Males]] [[Category:Creatures]] [[Category:Disney characters]] [[Category:Animated characters]] [[Category:Silent characters]] [[Category:Stitch! characters]]

[[Experiments]] ("cousins")}} '''Elastico''', also known as '''Experiment 345''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. He is designed to distract hostile forces with his clownish antics and elastic body. His one true place is with the circus. ==Background== ===Personality=== Elastico is a very playful, fun-loving experiment and treats just about anything like a game. He loves entertaining folks, sometimes breaking the rules for his own fun. Being a natural contortionist, he amuses himself by stretching his body into fun shapes or using them to pull little stunts or jokes on others. He can be a bit of a prankster, as he enjoys fooling around and teasing his enemies, often irritating them. Despite this, he can be very jumpy in immediate danger or if someone is trying to catch him. Also, he loves both of his families (his circus family and his ''[[Pelekai ʻohana|ʻohana]]'' with [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]], [[Stitch]], and the other experiments) very much. Elastico is generally very friendly and affectionate towards others. The one thing he dislikes more than anything is being grabbed or restrained, with the exception of hugs. He is also very terrified of [[Captain Gantu|Gantu]], screaming every time he sees him and grabbing onto Stitch's head when Gantu approaches. This is quite reasonable due to the fact that Elastico has been grabbed, choked, netted, kidnapped, pulled, squeezed, blasted, and shackled by Gantu. Despite this, he seems to have gotten over his fear by "[[Checkers (episode)|Checkers]]", as he was seen bravely rebelling against Gantu. ===Physical appearance=== Elastico is a green, furless, earless, clownish, roughly monkey-like creature with a small, stumpy tail, a large, red, round clown nose; white face and stomach, wide mouth, black eyes, neck frill, three huge tendrils on his head that resemble a jester's cap, and a purple spot on his stomach. He always wears a pink ruffled collar (like the ones that typical white-face circus clowns wear) around his neck, though it is unknown if it's removable. ===Powers and abilities=== True to his name, Elastico has rubbery properties. He can manipulatively stretch and bend any part of his body like taffy; this can range from him flattening himself until he is incredibly thin, to reshaping into anything from a parachute to a rubber raft. He uses this ability to perform amazing stunts and tricks. Like some of his cousins, Elastico can roll into a ball, though it acts more as a bouncy ball than the form Stitch and other experiments use. He can also inflate himself and float like a balloon. In the ''[[Stitch!]]'' anime, it is also revealed that Elastico can transform things into circus-related items and animals (dogs, monkeys, elephants, seals, etc.) after being transmutated by [[Dr. Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]. ==Appearances== ===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''=== Experiment 345 was the 345th genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Dr. Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to distract enemies by performing tricks with his elastic body. 345 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch|Experiment 626]]. All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of Kauai. At an unknown point after this, Experiment 345 was activated. 345 eventually found his way to an international circus, where he was taken in and named Elastico by the troupe's [[Ringmaster (Lilo & Stitch)|ringmaster]]. A newspaper article with Elastico's picture in it was almost used as a sandwich wrapper by [[Reuben|Experiment 625]]. When [[Captain Gantu|Gantu]] noticed the article on [[Gantu's Ship|his ship]], he snatched it and read the section. Reuben then revealed that Elastico had been activated two weeks ago, so Gantu headed off to the circus to capture the experiment. Meanwhile, [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]] was engrossed in a new hula dance, but ignored [[Stitch]] when he offered to help her. He later noticed Elastico riding atop a circus van, and after Lilo rebuked Stitch for his interference, he followed Elastico to the circus. There, Stitch disguised himself as a clown and attempted to capture Elastico, but the latter teased Stitch and turned the whole chase into a game. Eventually, Elastico calmed down when Stitch grabbed him and called him "cousin". As the entire audience began cheering for Stitch, he was pulled onto the stage and praised by Elastico's ringmaster, who nicknamed him "The Incredible Indestructorado". However, at that moment, Gantu barged in, strangled Elastico, and stuffed him into a [[Net Cannon|net]] before fleeing. Stitch revealed that Gantu had kidnapped Elastico, much to the ringmaster's dismay. He then mentioned how Stitch stole the show with his incredible stunts and even invited him to perform in Elastico's stead, to which Stitch happily accepted. He later met the circus troupe, where, after putting on an amazing show, he signed a contract permitting him to travel with the circus. Meanwhile, Gantu tried to teleport Elastico to [[Dr. Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]], but the experiment put up quite a fight and proved difficult to control. Reuben wagered a Monte Cristo sandwich on the ordeal, although Gantu soon disabled Elastico by blasting him and put him in shackles. However, he stretched out of the cuffs and under the teleport chamber just before the transfer could be completed. An angry Hämsterviel then contacted Gantu, thinking the latter was pranking him by sending him empty shackles, much to Gantu's shock and confusion. Elastico somehow packaged himself and then shipped himself back to the circus, reuniting with his ringmaster. When Lilo later discovered that Stitch had run away with the circus, she paid him a visit and attempted to make amends. Just then, Gantu attacked and tried to take Elastico back, but was thwarted by Lilo and Stitch, as well as the entire circus troupe. As the circus prepared to leave for Las Vegas, Lilo and Stitch made up. When the ringmaster learned that Stitch had a family of his own, the former voided the contract on a technicality (as Stitch had previously signed it with his own name, rather than the nickname he was given by the ringmaster) and let Stitch be with his ''[[Pelekai ʻohana|ʻohana]]''. After Stitch said his goodbyes, he and Lilo decided that Elastico's one true place was staying with the circus. Elastico was one of the experiments in "[[Checkers (episode)|Checkers]]" that joined Stitch in a rebellion against Gantu. Gantu even put Elastico on his head (thinking the latter was [[Checkers]]). In "[[Remmy (episode)|Remmy]]", Elastico was one of the experiments in Lilo's dream. ===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''=== The first 624 experiments, including Elastico, were rounded up by [[Leroy]] and taken to a stadium to be destroyed. However, [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]], [[Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben]], and [[Captain Gantu|Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed. Elastico participated in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]] by strangling attacking Leroys with his elastic body. However, the Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle, but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben, and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe. Elastico joins them for the song by playing the trombone. ===''[[Stitch!]]''=== Elastico made an appearance in the ''Stitch!'' anime where [[Dr. Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]] modified him with the ability to transform things into circus-related items and animals (dogs, monkeys, elephants, seals, etc.) in order to turn [[Stitch]] into a harmless little puppy, thus making him easier to capture. It is also revealed that Elastico is capable of speaking fluently. However, [[Yuna Kamihara|Yuna]] was turned into a dog by mistake, and Stitch was unaware that it was actually her until he later found her in a circus tent being tortured to do tricks for the circus. Elastico later appeared as one of the experiments who helped Stitch fight [[Dark End]]. He also appeared in the special ''Stitch and the Planet of Sand''. ==Gallery== {{Gallerylink}} ==Trivia== *Elastico's number was never revealed in [[Elastico (episode)|his debut]], but his number Wall crawling |paraphernalia = Laser |status = Active |siblings = Each other (Siamese twin brothers) |creator = [[Jumba Jookiba]] |family = [[Experiments]] ("cousins")}} '''Swapper''', also known as '''Experiment 355''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. They are designed to switch individuals' minds; it is possible for them to swap more than two individuals at once, and they will only switch them back by choice. ==Background== ===Personality=== Because Swapper is two heads on the same body, they are two conjoined twin beings cooperating as one, though their personalities mirror each other; they can be indecisive at times, but usually work well together. An example is when [[Stitch]] in [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]]'s body asked the two-headed cousin to switch their minds back, Swapper's left and right, after hesitating, blew a raspberry in response. The two enjoy messing with individuals by swapping their brains and refuse to switch them back unless threatened. However, Swapper will eventually switch individuals' minds back into their original bodies when both heads choose to do so (or when given "proper motivation"). ===Physical appearance=== Swapper is a green lizard-like experiment with two heads on a conjoined body at the rear. Both sides of the body have a set of arms, but only one pair of legs and purple markings extending to each. They have three purple-tipped tendrils on each head. ===Powers and abilities=== Swapper can emit a green ray from each head's eyes once each head is pointed at one of two individuals. The ray will swap the minds and voices of the targets, as well as vice versa, and the only means of returning to normal is through Swapper choosing to do so. It even works if one or both targets are on a video screen, or if Swapper is encased in clear glass (unless the glass is covered from the experiment's view). Although they normally use their power on two people, Swapper isn't limited to this specifically, since they were able to hit four beings at once. They can also scale walls and roll into a wheel-like shape. ==Appearances== ===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''=== Experiment 355 was the 355th genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Dr. Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. They were designed to swap any two (or more) individuals' minds. According to Jumba, 355 once swapped the former and his wife for an entire month, which led to a divorce in the end. 355 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch|Experiment 626]]. All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of Kauai. At an unknown point after this, Experiment 355 was activated and captured by [[Captain Gantu|Gantu]]. When Gantu was about to teleport 355 to [[Dr. Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]], 355 got loose and swapped Gantu and Hämsterviel's minds, allowing 355 to escape. Hämsterviel in Gantu's body then decided to go AWOL and recapture 355, but refused to have 355 switch their minds back afterwards, although Gantu in Hämsterviel's body protested. Sometime later, [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]] and [[Stitch]] encountered 355 in [[Kokaua Town|town]] and managed to capture them in a [[Prison Capsule|containment orb]], but 355 was able to swap their minds in the process. After 355, named Swapper, refused to switch Lilo and Stitch's minds back, they took the two-headed cousin [[Lilo's House|home]], where [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] covered up Swapper's container with a towel to prevent the latter from using their mind-swapping power on the former. When [[Pleakley]] removed the towel, Swapper switched his and Jumba's minds as well, forcing Lilo's dysfunctional ''[[Pelekai ʻohana|ʻohana]]'' to throw a "Lilo's Not Weird" party that she hosted earlier. As soon as [[Victoria]], [[Mertle Edmonds|Mertle]], and [[Elena, Teresa, and Yuki|the hula girls]] showed up, the four attempted to act like the other's self as they entertained their guests, which proved to be difficult for all of them. Later, Gantu with Hämsterviel's mind arrived at the Pelekais' house (after being tipped by Hämsterviel with Gantu's mind) for Swapper, where a fight ensued during which they switched Lilo, Stitch, Jumba, and Pleakley's minds again, though each one was in someone else's body. After Hämsterviel in Gantu's body was defeated, Swapper switched Lilo, Stitch, Jumba, and Pleakley's minds back into their original bodies, and they were then forced to do the same with Gantu and Hämsterviel's minds as well, on account of Jumba threatening to feed them Pleakley's disgusting cuisine (namely Aunt Pleakley's famous chocolate green bean surprise) for dinner. Afterwards, Lilo and Stitch decided to find Swapper's one true place, though it was never revealed. ===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''=== The first 624 experiments, including Swapper, were rounded up by [[Leroy]] and taken to a stadium to be destroyed. However, [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]], [[Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben]], and [[Captain Gantu|Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed. Swapper participated in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]], but it is unknown what they did. The Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle, but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben, and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe. Swapper joins them for the song by playing the keyboard piano. ===''[[Stitch!]]''=== Swapper made an appearance in the ''Stitch!'' anime where [[Dr. Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]] used them to switch [[Stitch]] and [[Hiroman]]'s bodies. It is also revealed that Swapper is capable of speaking fluently. Until they could find Swapper again, Hiroman needed to figure out how to use Stitch's abilities to take on [[Heat]] when he attacked. After Heat, [[Captain Gantu|Gantu]], and [[Reuben]] were defeated, [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] made a request for Swapper to swap Stitch and Hiroman back into their original bodies, but instead of obeying Jumba's plea, they switched everyone's bodies again. Eventually, Swapper was presumably reverted back to normal, then dehydrated back into an experiment pod and locked in Jumba's vault. Eventually, Jumba grabbed their pod to help Stitch in his fight against [[Dark End]], but Swapper wasn't one of the experiments that was activated. They later appeared in the special ''Stitch and the Planet of Sand''. ==Gallery== {{Gallerylink}} ==Trivia== *Swapper's appearance is a reference to Siamese twins of people or animals. *Swapper was activated off-screen. *Swapper is one of the few known experiments whose powers Stitch is vulnerable to. **He is also one of the few known experiments whose powers Lilo falls victim to. *Jumba explained that Swapper once swapped him and his wife for entire month, which taught them so much about each other before they got divorced. *Swapper is one of the three known experiments that has more than one head, the other two being [[Forehead]] and [[627]], having four heads and two heads respectively, though 627 usually only appears with one head. *Similar to [[Splodyhead]], [[Clink]], and [[Plasmoid]], Swapper has six limbs. However, unlike those three, Swapper does not use all six for locomotion. *Swapper is one of the few experiments to not have their one true place revealed. *Swapper's ability to {{WikipediaLink|Body swap|swap victims' bodies}} is a very common trope seen in various fictional media, also known as a [https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/FreakyFridayFlip ''Freaky Friday'' Flip], named after [[wikipedia:Freaky Friday|the 1972 novel]] and its [[Freaky Friday (1976)|three]] [[Freaky Friday (1995)|film]] [[Freaky Friday (2003)|adaptations]] (also produced by [[The Walt Disney Company|Disney]]). ==External links== *{{L&S|Swapper (355)}} {{Lilo & Stitch}} [[Category:Lilo & Stitch Experiments]] [[Category:Lilo & Stitch characters]] [[Category:Aliens]] [[Category:Creatures]] [[Category:Males]] [[Category:Disney characters]] [[Category:Monsters]] [[Category:Multi-headed characters]] [[Category:Animated characters]] [[Category:Silent characters]] [[Category:Twins and Triplets]]

[[Experiments]] ("cousins")}} '''Manners''', also known as '''Experiment 358''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. He is designed to give people painfully perfect manners. With a wave of dust from his fingers, his victims become too polite to fight back. His one true place is with [[Mrs. Hasagawa]] as one of her "cats". ==Personality== Unlike most experiments, Manners does not cause actual mischief nor chaos. Nevertheless, as part of his programming, he is polite to a fault and doesn't like it when others argue or fight. Thus, he will use his powers to force them to be polite and get along. However, he is not mean-spirited and simply wants everyone to be polite and behave. ==Appearances== ===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''=== Experiment 358 was the 358th genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Dr. Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to make people too polite to fight back against hostile forces. 358 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch|Experiment 626]]. All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of Kauai. Against statistically unlikely (but not impossible) odds, several experiment pods landed in one location: [[Mrs. Hasagawa]]'s yard, 358's pod being one of them. At an unknown point, [[Mrs. Hasagawa]] mistook 358's pod for an apricot and washed it, activating the experiment. However, as 358 was not a very evil or destructive experiment, he was able to live a peaceful life with her, due to the latter seeing the former as a mere stray cat who needed a home. When [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]] and [[Stitch]] discovered that Mrs. Hasagawa kept several experiments as pets, they thought they were a danger to her and, along with [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] and [[Pleakley]], decided to capture them all. Earlier, 358 politely greeted Lilo and Stitch at Mrs. Hasagawa's door and let them in. Jumba and Pleakley started arguing over who was going to capture 358. Seeing this, the experiment demonstrated his power of making people overly polite on them. Despite Jumba and Pleakley being too polite to capture experiments, 358 was [[Prison Capsule|captured]] anyway by unknown means. 358 and the other experiments were about to be taken away, but were returned to Mrs. Hasagawa when Lilo and Stitch saw how much she cared for them. 358 was then named Manners. ===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''=== The first 624 experiments, including Manners, were rounded up by [[Leroy]] and taken to a stadium to be destroyed. However, [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]], [[Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben]], and [[Captain Gantu|Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed. Manners participated in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]], but it is unknown what he did. However, it is presumed that he would have been able to use his powers to make attacking Leroys too polite to fight. The Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle, but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben, and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe. ==Trivia== *Manners' appearance and [[United Kingdom|British]] accent are a likely reference to most classic British butlers. *Manners was activated off-screen. *The first time Manners' spines appear when he bows, they are yellow; then when the scene changes to where he is beside the door, his spikes are black. *Manners is one of the few known experiments that can speak fluently. *Manners is one of the few experiments to not appear in the group photo at the end of ''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''. ==Gallery== ===Screenshots=== Come in and be our guests.png|"Do come in. [[Experiments]] ("cousins")}} '''Drowsy''', also known as '''Experiment 360''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. He is designed to cause populations to fall into a near-permanent sleep by simply bleating; only spraying water in the victim's face will awaken them, and other experiments are less vulnerable to his bleats. His one true place is putting insomniacs to sleep. ==Background== ===Physical appearance=== Drowsy is a grayish light-blue sheep-like experiment with striped ears, short arms and legs, and black fingers and toes. He is able to walk on his hind legs. ===Powers and abilities=== Drowsy's bleat causes anyone who hears it to enter a near-permanent sleep. ==Appearances== ===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''=== Experiment 360 was the 360th genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Dr. Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to use his sleep-inducing bleat to cause his victims to instantly enter a near-permanent sleep. 360 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch |Experiment 626]]. All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of Kauai. 360's pod was one of the twelve experiment pods recovered by [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]] and [[Stitch]] in "[[Drowsy (episode)|Drowsy]]". His was one of the final four pods (among [[Stopgo|102]], [[Experiments#2-Series: Technological and scientific|274]], and [[Nosox|204]]) that [[Pleakley]], with some assistance from Stitch, cataloged after being convinced to do so by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]]. Lilo had become restless lately while catching experiments with Stitch, so [[Nani Pelekai|Nani]] threatened to ban her from doing any future experiment hunting if she was unable to fulfill her duties or be attentive. Stitch then attempted to get Lilo to fall asleep that night. Eventually, Stitch activated 360 and used the latter's bleat to put Lilo to sleep. However, Lilo was still asleep the next morning when Nani called for her, and Stitch couldn't wake her up. To try and solve the problem, Stitch tried to make Lilo seem awake by putting sunglasses on her, mimicking her voice, and moving her around like a puppet all over [[Kokaua Town|town]]. Meanwhile, 360 escaped and was chased throughout Kauai by Jumba and Pleakley, while 360 put everyone he encountered to sleep by bleating. Pleakley initially caught 360 in his purse, but then opened it to put [[Captain Gantu|Gantu]] to sleep when the latter was looking for the experiment. At that point, however, 360 jumped out as Gantu fell heavily on Pleakley. Jumba then scolded Pleakley for letting 360 escape. Gantu was later woken up by a bunch of people on [[Lahui Beach|the beach]], who thought he was a beached whale and dumped water over him (though they fled in fear after hearing him talk). He then received a call from [[Dr. Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]] who demanded 360 from Gantu. Stitch was unable to wake Lilo up all day until Jumba revealed that the cure to 360's powers was to spray water in the victim's face. After Lilo was awakened, Stitch told her that she had to meet someone at the [[Kauai Airport|airport]]. Because she'd been asleep at the time, Lilo started to worry, but Jumba reassured her that Stitch had taken care of all her appointments. Later, after a long chase, Gantu and [[Reuben|Experiment 625]] captured 360 in a duffel bag and guarded the [[Birds of Paradise Hotel]]. However, when they tried to use 360 to kidnap [[Regis Philbin]] (the man from the airport) while posing as bellboys, Lilo and Stitch were there for Regis since he had disembarked and protected him in every way they could. Lilo eventually recaptured 360, named him Drowsy, and let Regis spend the night at the [[Lilo's House|Pelekai residence]]. In the end, Drowsy used his sleep-inducing powers to send Regis and everyone in Lilo's ''[[Pelekai ʻohana|ʻohana]]'' to sleep. In "[[PJ (episode)|PJ]]", Lilo used Drowsy to put Stitch to sleep after claiming he had trouble sleeping lately, allowing her to release [[PJ (Lilo & Stitch)|PJ]] and use him to avenge her strict substitute teacher. Strangely, however, Stitch woke up on his own. In "[[Ploot (episode)|Ploot]]", Drowsy was one of the second team of experiments (along with [[Finder]] and [[Babyfier]]) formed to try and stop [[Ploot]]. However, Ploot was easily able to defeat them, forcing the three experiments to retreat. In "[[Remmy (episode)|Remmy]]", Drowsy was one of the experiments in Lilo's dream. ===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''=== The first 624 experiments, including Drowsy, were rounded up by [[Leroy]] and taken to a stadium to be destroyed. However, [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]], [[Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben]], and [[Captain Gantu|Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed. It is unknown whether or not Drowsy participated in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]]. The Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle, but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben, and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe. ==Gallery== {{Gallerylink}} ==Trivia== *Drowsy's sleep-inducing bleat and sheep-like appearance are most likely derived from {{WikipediaLink|Counting sheep|the mental exercise of counting sheep}} in an attempt to fall asleep. *He is one of the few known experiments whose powers Lilo falls victim to. *A recurring irony has occurred with Drowsy. Stitch originally used him to get Lilo to fall asleep, and in his [[PJ (episode)|second appearance]], Lilo used him to put Stitch to sleep. **Stitch wasn't initially affected when Drowsy put Lilo to sleep, though when Stitch was put to sleep by Drowsy, he somehow managed to wake up on his own without having to be splashed by water, possibly indicating that other experiments are not affected as much. *Drowsy's [[Experiment Pods|pod]] color is yellow. *The [[Experiment Pod Container]] describes Drowsy as: "Experiment 360. Primary function: Sleep inducer." *Oddly, when Drowsy's image is reflected off of Stitch's eyes in ''[[The Origin of Stitch]]'', he is not yawning for some reason. It is possible that Drowsy's yawning image was taken from ''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''. ==External links== *{{L&S|Drowsy (360)}} {{Lilo & Stitch}} [[Category:Males]] [[Category:Lilo & Stitch characters]] [[Category:Lilo & Stitch Experiments]] [[Category:Aliens]] [[Category:Creatures]] [[Category:Disney characters]] [[Category:Sheep]] [[Category:Animated characters]] [[Category:Silent characters]] [[Category:Neutral characters]]

Flight |status = Active |creator = [[Jumba Jookiba]] |family = [[Experiments]] ("cousins")}} '''Phantasmo''', also known as '''Experiment 375''', is an illegal [[Experiments|genetic experiment]] created by [[Jumba Jookiba]] and a character in the [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|''Lilo & Stitch'' franchise]]. He is designed to take possession of inanimate objects and, through them, create utter chaos. Being ghost-like, he is intangible and can phase through obstacles, thus making him virtually uncatchable. His one true place is keeping the Macki Macaw animatronic functional at the [[Macki Macaw's|titular pizza restaurant]]. ==Background== ===Personality=== Phantasmo is a mischievous experiment who enjoys wreaking havoc. He also has a tendency to gloat by laughing in a squeaky voice and is rather quite smart too. When possessing an object, he tries to do so when nobody is around and will act as the object he is possessing to avoid being exposed. Due to advanced programming, he would dispose of those who discover his true identity. Being always on the move, jumping from object to object, he craves attention. This is ultimately exploited in order to get him to perform for attention instead of causing chaos. ===Physical appearance=== Phantasmo is a green, semi-transparent ghostlike experiment with short arms, a large conehead with two light green stripes, a koala-like face, long rabbit-like ears, and dark pupil-less eyes. Instead of legs, Phantasmo has a continuous wisp-like tail. ===Powers and abilities=== Phantasmo's spectral nature gives him abilities commonly associated with those of spirits. He can possess any inanimate object and bring it to life and can also phase through anything, making him impossible to keep in one place. As a ghostly experiment, he is virtually uncatchable by conventional means (including [[Net Cannon|nets]] and [[Prison Capsule|capsules]]), thanks to his intangibility. ==Appearances== ===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''=== Experiment 375 was the 375th genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Dr. Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to possess inanimate objects and cause massive mischief and chaos through them. 375 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch|Experiment 626]]. All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of Kauai. 375's pod eventually made its way into a pearl oyster inside the crane game at [[Macki Macaw's|Macki Macaw's pizzeria]]. [[Stitch]] played the claw game and won the oyster, but a glitch in the machine caused him to shake it in frustration, prompting [[Nani Pelekai|Nani]] to intervene and scold Stitch. After the oyster freed itself, despite Stitch's misconduct, the employee let [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]] keep the prize, and she and Stitch took it [[Lilo's House|home]] with them. When Lilo tried to give Stitch a bath (after Nani mentioned the word "bath"), the latter fled and hid in the laundry hamper, but she tricked Stitch into coming out and then dragged him to the bathroom. There, an incident with the bathtub, which overflowed after Lilo immersed Stitch in the water, resulted in the oyster opening and the pod inside getting wet, activating 375. That night, 375 wreaked havoc in the kitchen. When Stitch was alerted, he attempted to save [[Pleakley]]'s dishes, but 375 made Stitch lose his balance and shatter them. 375 then possessed [[Scrump]] and used the doll to paint Nani's face green, sabotage [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]]'s [[Jumba's Computer|experiment analyzer]], steal Pleakley's begonia, break Lilo's record player, brush Nani's toothbrush on Stitch's toes, and frame Stitch for it all. The next morning, Nani, thinking Stitch was the culprit, threw the latter outside and made Lilo chain him up as punishment until Nani returned from work. However, Stitch noticed 375 using Scrump again to unravel Lilo's [[Elvis Presley|Elvis]] videotapes. Stitch broke free and attacked Lilo's doll, only to arouse her suspicion. When Stitch was later being prosecuted, he saw 375 (still inside Scrump) wink at him, causing Stitch to lash out at Lilo's doll. Later that day, while 375 was attempting to break Pleakley's flower pot to get Stitch into deeper trouble, Lilo caught him right in the act. 375 revealed himself and possessed a rope, with which it tied Lilo, Jumba, and Pleakley up. He then repossessed Scrump and prepared to execute the three with Jumba's [[Plasma Blaster|blaster]], but a wary and vigilant Stitch ambushed 375 and freed his ''[[Pelekai ʻohana|ʻohana]]''. While the four searched for 375, he possessed a vacuum cleaner and almost sucked Pleakley up with it. Lilo and Stitch then made a vain attempt to [[Prison Capsule|capture]] the intangible experiment, forcing 375 to retreat into [[Kokaua Town]]. After a long pursuit through town, when 375 turned the tables, Nani gave Lilo and Stitch a lift in her jeep and led 375 to Macki Macaw's, where he used the claw machine to trap Stitch. The former then chased Lilo backstage and possessed the Macki Macaw animatronic that had malfunctioned earlier. After Lilo raised the curtain, 375 put on a show for an audience. 375, christened Phantasmo, was then convinced by Lilo that using the animatronic parrot to entertain children and receive adoration was a better way of gaining attention than causing chaos, thus rehabilitating him now that he had found his one true place. Phantasmo made a cameo at the end of "[[Snooty (episode)|Snooty]]" on [[Captain Gantu|Gantu]]'s TV set continuing his duty inside the Macki Macaw animatronic as the ex-captain watched the show with great interest. ===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''=== The first 624 experiments, including Phantasmo, were rounded up by [[Leroy]] and taken to a stadium to be destroyed. However, [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]], [[Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben]], and [[Captain Gantu|Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed. Phantasmo participated in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]], but it is unknown what he did. Although he was seen among some of the Leroys, it is presumed that he wouldn't have been able to be very effective, due to the fact that his powers are deemed useless. The Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle, but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben, and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe. ===''[[Stitch!]]''=== Phantasmo made a special guest appearance in the ''Stitch!'' segment "[[w:c:liloandstitch:Kung Fu Dragon Pleak Lee|Kung Fu Dragon Pleak Lee]]". ==Gallery== {{Gallerylink}} ==Trivia== *Phantasmo was first revealed in a DVD bonus feature of ''[[Stitch! The Movie]]'' in the experiment gallery. *An early version of Phantasmo appears on an old downloadable activity printout for ''Stitch! The Movie''. This beta design depicts him with a rounder Stitch-like head, a round nose, tufts of fur on his head and chest, and two short antennae. **This design is confirmed to be him through [https://wendygriebstoryboards.blogspot.com/2022/01/lilo-and-stitch-phantasmo.html storyboards of his episode] by storyboard artist Wendy Grieb. **It is likely that his design was changed because he resembled Stitch too much. *Phantasmo is clearly a spectral being, as he possesses intangibility and the ability to phase through obstacles, thus making him the only experiment that cannot be restrained or captured. **Due to this, it is unknown how Jumba managed to create him, let alone dehydrate him into an [[Experiment Pods|experiment pod]]. **This would come into question in ''[[Leroy & Stitch]]'' on how he was captured by a Leroy clone. Also, he was seen being chased by another Leroy clone with a [[Plasma Blaster|plasma gun]], despite his inability to sustain physical injuries. *Phantasmo, [[Fudgy]], [[Remmy]], [[Tickle-Tummy]], and [[Witch (Lilo & Stitch)|Witch]] are the only known experiments to have arms but no legs. **Interestingly, excluding Fudgy, all of these experiments are capable of levitation. Remmy is always seen levitating. Phantasmo and Witch primarily levitate but often possess objects or living beings to move by other means. Tickle-Tummy is also able to levitate, but has been seen bouncing as well. *Phantasmo, [[Glitch]], and Witch are all capable of possession, albeit in different capacities: Phantasmo can possess any inanimate object, Glitch possesses technology, and Witch can possess living beings. *Phantasmo has the ability to speak fluently, but he only does so after possessing the Macki Macaw animatronic. Also, he replaces the animatronic's pre-recorded voice with that of his own and inexplicably knows who Macki Macaw and the Hammerheads are. *Due to being voiced by [[Nancy Cartwright]], his voice is similar to [[w:c:simpsons:Bart Simpson|Bart Simpson]]. *As Phantasmo's possession of objects brings them to life, the possessed objects are able to perform actions that they normally cannot do. **Despite being lightweight and having a flexible body, [[Scrump]] was able to not only move "herself", but "she" also gains the strength to lift or pull objects, such as a cloth that had Pleakley's plant on it. The same goes to a bunch of bananas in the Pelekais' kitchen that Phantasmo possesses shortly after his activation, as he uses them to open a microwave oven's door. **A traffic light sprouted arms and legs, grabbing some coconuts and running off until Stitch runs it over with the [[X-Buggy]], destroying it. **A tiki statue from a store facade was able to move its own limbs and run off. He is designed to hypnotize individuals into obeying the next order or suggestion they hear; snapping one's fingers will break the victim's trance. His one true place is hypnotizing guests at children's parties. ==Background== ===Personality=== Swirly is mute and mostly docile, usually staring off into space when not using his powers. However, he is quite active with his hypnosis, as it is performed at the most inadequate of times to humiliate others. Although generally harmless, Swirly is sort of apathetic to whoever is unlucky enough to fall under his hypnosis as he just leaves whoever is affected to their own devices. ===Physical appearance=== Swirly is a small koala-like experiment with desaturated blue fur and a small doglike tail. Most of the time, he appears hunched and expressionless. His head and facial features are very large in proportion to his body, although there is a small antenna on the middle of his head. His eyes are black and pupil-less (but become white swirling lines when using his powers) and has large rabbit-like ears. ===Powers and abilities=== Swirly possesses the ability to hypnotize anyone who looks into his eyes, forcing them to obey the next order or suggestion they hear, by making his eyes swirl. His victims will snap out of their trances once they hear someone snap their fingers; also, if no order or suggestion is heard within a few minutes, the effect wears off. ==Appearances== ===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''=== Experiment 383 was the 383rd genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Jacques von Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to hypnotize his victims into obeying the next order or suggestion they heard. 383 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch |Experiment 626]]. All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of Kauai, with 383's pod landing on a [[Lahui Beach|beach]] shore. When a small wave washed over the shore, 383's pod got wet, activating the experiment. 383 then hypnotized a surfer, who had witnessed his activation, and left the scene. After hypnotizing [[Ice Cream Man|a tourist]] (who, based on a comment from [[Mertle Edmonds|Mertle]], began clucking like a chicken), 383 was discovered by [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]] and [[Stitch]], but just before they could take action, [[Captain Gantu|Gantu]] ambushed them and captured 383 in a [[Prison Capsule|containment orb]]. 383 was soon caught in a fight between Lilo, Stitch, and Gantu, which ended with Lilo and Stitch retrieving 383. Gantu was then forced to flee from a swarm of bees after Stitch upset their hive. Lilo and Stitch took 383, named Swirly, back to their [[Lilo's House|house]] and learned about his powers from [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]]. They then tried to hide Swirly from a very strict [[Nani Pelekai|Nani]], who prohibited any of Jumba's experiments besides Stitch, when she returned from work. However, in the ensuing chaos, Swirly managed to hypnotize both Lilo (who, based on a suggestion from [[Pleakley]], started behaving like her rival Mertle) and Stitch (who, based on a comment from the hypnotized Lilo, became an obsessive fan of the reality show ''Look at This!'') and escaped outside. Gantu later recaptured Swirly and was briefly hypnotized by the latter back at [[Gantu's Ship|his ship]]. This fascinated [[Reuben|Experiment 625]], who then amused himself by making Gantu do silly stuff. Even [[Dr. Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]] became intrigued after seeing this and toyed with Gantu a bit before snapping him out of his trance. Later, Gantu traveled to the TV studio, where he used Swirly to hypnotize the manager into putting him on the ''Look at This!'' show, which was part of Hämsterviel's clever scheme. Gantu then planned to have Swirly turn the show's viewers into slaves. Lilo and Stitch, who just so happened to be on the show, were still under Swirly's hypnosis from before. Back home, Jumba, who was watching the show on TV out of curiosity, soon found out what was going on. He then came to the show in person and managed to snap Lilo and Stitch out of their trances so they could rescue Swirly. Gantu prepared to hypnotize the show's viewers into slaves using Swirly, but Lilo and Stitch pulled the plug on Gantu's charade by recapturing Swirly. He later found his one true place hypnotizing guests at a children's party that Stitch had won from being on the show, with Mertle becoming one of Swirly's victims. In "[[The Asteroid]]", Swirly was one of the six experiments that Stitch convinced to come with him and Lilo to save Earth from an approaching asteroid. Along the journey, Swirly hypnotized the extraterrestrial asteroid squatter to prevent him from distracting Lilo and the others as they safely diverted the asteroid using the [[Jumba's Ship|ship]]'s hyperdrive engine. ===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''=== The first 624 experiments, including Swirly, were rounded up by [[Leroy]] and taken to a stadium to be destroyed. However, [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]], [[Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben]], and [[Captain Gantu|Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed. Swirly participated in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]] by hypnotizing attacking Leroys. However, the Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle, but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben, and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's failsafe. ===''[[Stitch!]]''=== Swirly made a cameo appearance in the ''Stitch!'' anime as one of the experiments in [[Dr. Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s [[Prison Asteroid K-37|prison cell]]. He made another appearance where Hämsterviel used him to hypnotize [[Stitch]] into fighting for the alien scientist. [[Captain Gantu|Gantu]] is also hypnotized by Swirly; this time, making him believe he is a scared chicken. Hämsterviel notes that he should have hypnotized Gantu sooner and decides to keep him in a trance. For the rest of the episode, Gantu is seen in the background acting like a chicken and even tries to lay an egg. This episode also featured [[Plasmoid]] and [[Splodyhead]] who helped combat Stitch while he was under Swirly's hypnosis. Swirly later appeared in the special ''Stitch and the Planet of Sand'', where he was captured by Hämsterviel. After breaking free, Swirly finds Gantu and hypnotizes him once again. This time, he makes Gantu destroy several of Hämsterviel's robots. Later, Swirly is seen at a party with the rest of the experiments, playing cards with Gantu who is still hypnotized. ==Gallery== {{Gallerylink}} ==Trivia== *In [[Swirly (episode)|his debut]], Swirly's fur color is green, but in promotional artwork and all of his other animated appearances, including ''[[Stitch!]]'', his fur color is grayish blue. *When Swirly hypnotizes the [[Ice Cream Man]], his eyes can be seen. *Swirly is one of the few known experiments whose powers Stitch is vulnerable to. **He is also one of the few known experiments whose powers Lilo falls victim to. *Swirly's [[Experiment Pods|pod]] color is yellow. *Swirly's head, antenna, and ears appear in the online game ''[[Jumba's Lab]]''. ==External links== *{{L&S|Swirly (383)}} {{Lilo & Stitch}} [[Category:Males]] [[Category:Lilo & Stitch characters]] [[Category:Lilo & Stitch Experiments]] [[Category:Creatures]] [[Category:Aliens]] [[Category:Disney characters]] [[Category:Animated characters]] [[Category:Silent characters]] [[Category:Stitch! characters]]

He is designed to cause local populations to argue with each other so they do not notice someone taking over their planet. If the afflicted individuals count to ten, their belligerence will dissolve. His one true place is with [[Wizard Kelly]], making his professional wrestlers fight more convincingly. ==Background== ===Personality=== Spats is sneaky, clever, and cunning and will do whatever it takes to start an argument. He loves to cause a ruckus and provoke a fight or quarrel. He is also a good actor and does a great job of faking being innocent and cute to get what he wants or to trick individuals. ===Physical appearance=== Spats is a small, yellow squirrel/cat-like experiment with two short antennae above his eyes, black-violet eyes, a small red-orange round nose, a wide mouth with sharp catlike fangs and a green tongue, and two prongs on the tip of his long bushy tail (seen when fully outstretched). He has orange spots on his forehead, a white belly, and orange markings on his back. ===Powers and abilities=== Spats can fire a yellow ray from the prongs on the tip of his tail that causes any two individuals zapped to constantly argue with each other. The sound of a bell is heard when this happens. ==Appearances== ===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''=== Experiment 397 was the 397th genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Dr. Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to instigate arguments between individuals. 397 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch|Experiment 626]]. All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of Kauai, with 397's pod landing in the window of [[Jumba's Ship|Jumba's ship]]. When [[the Proud Family]] visits Kauai for a vacation, [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]], [[Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], and [[Pleakley]] invite their guests to stay at "[[Jumba & Pleakley's Bed & Not Breakfast]]" hotel. [[Penny Proud]] gets more acquainted with Lilo and Stitch, while [[Oscar Proud]] complains about the hotel's accommodations. Later, [[Suga Mama]] soaks herself in a hot tub, while her dog [[Puff]] sleeps on a throw rug. Meanwhile, a squirrel appears inside one of the windows of [[Jumba's Ship|Jumba's ship]] and notices 397's experiment pod. The squirrel mistakes the pod for a nut and attempts to eat it. When it finds out it could not eat the pod, the squirrel throws it into a bowl of bath bombs. Shortly after, Suga Mama reaches for a bath bomb, but takes out 397's pod instead. Mistaking the pod for a bath bomb, Suga Mama drops it into the bathtub, activating 397, named Spats. He then zaps the squirrel and Puff, causing the two animals to fight. Spats causes more mischief in [[Kokaua Town|town]] by zapping numerous pairs who end up fighting as well. His victims include [[BeBe & CeCe Proud|BeBe and CeCe]], followed by Oscar and [[Trudy Proud]], then Jumba and [[Mr. Cooper]], and later Lilo and Penny. A [[Charles and Mary|newlywed couple]] also becomes affected by Spats' argument-inducing ray. Elsewhere, Stitch notices Spats being pursued by [[Captain Gantu|Gantu]]. However, he manages to evade both Gantu and Stitch, and eventually hitches a ride in the back of a jeep that Pleakley is driving. Spats then teases Stitch when the latter is unable to catch up with him. After making a vain attempt to break up Penny and Lilo's conflict, Stitch chases after Spats in [[Nani Pelekai|Nani]]'s [[X-Buggy|dune buggy]], taking the feuding girls with him. Later, Stitch manages to track Spats down to an outdoor wrestling match, where the two cousins face off against each other on the roof of the arena. After a long battle between both experiments, Spats falls off the roof and into Penny's arms. She is angered by his presence at first, but after noticing Spats' cuteness, she starts to soften up. When Penny tries to talk to Lilo, the latter still wants to fight with her. Fortunately, Penny manages to resist her urge to fight by counting to ten and then convinces Lilo to do the same, which she does. After Lilo and Penny make up, the former is able to relieve the other brawling pairs by telling everyone through an overhead microphone to count to ten after Gantu, who was wrestling with Suga Mama all this time (due to Spats zapping them when Suga Mama attacked Gantu after he threatened to take Spats away from Penny earlier), went down for the count. The next day, Lilo and Stitch find Spats his one true place with [[Wizard Kelly]]. He uses Spats to make his international wrestlers fight more convincingly. Penny reveals to Lilo about having a perfect newspaper article for her school, and she along with the rest of the Proud Family leave on good terms. ===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''=== The first 624 experiments, including Spats, were rounded up by [[Leroy]] and taken to a stadium to be destroyed. However, [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]], [[Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben]] and [[Captain Gantu|Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed. Spats participated in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]] probably by making attacking Leroys fight each other. However, the Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe. ==Gallery== {{Gallerylink}} ==Trivia== *Stitch and Pleakley are the only main characters to not get zapped by Spats. *He is one of the few known experiments whose powers Lilo falls victim to. *Spats' [[Experiment Pods|pod]] color is yellow. *Spats, [[Morpholomew]], and [[Lax]] are the only experiments that debuted in crossovers. *The [[Experiment Pod Container]] describes Spats as: "Experiment 397. He is designed to use his tentacles to squeeze the life out of his victims. ==Background== ===Physical appearance=== Huggo is a large purple/blue cephalopod-like experiment, but with six tentacles and two eye stalks. ===Powers and abilities=== Huggo can squeeze the life out of enemies by using his tentacles. ==Appearances== ===''[[Stitch! The Movie]]''=== Experiment 489 was the 489th genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Dr. Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. He was designed to squeeze the life out of his victims with his tentacles. 489 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch|Experiment 626]]. All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of Kauai, with 489's pod landing on top of a buoy. Later, a tidal wave splashed over the buoy, activating the experiment. ===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''=== At an unknown point after this, Experiment 489 was presumably captured, tamed, and named Huggo. ===''[[The Origin of Stitch]]''=== Huggo was one of the experiments that was gliding on the screen, but he is 144 instead of 489. ===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''=== All 624 experiments, including Huggo, were rounded up by [[Leroy]] and taken to a stadium to be destroyed. However, Lilo, Stitch, Jumba, Pleakley, Reuben, and Gantu arrived before the experiments could be destroyed. It is unknown whether or not Huggo participated in the following battle between the experiments and the [[Leroy Clones|Leroy clones]]. The Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle, but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben, and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe. ==Trivia== *Huggo is one of only two 4-series experiments that have their image, name, number, and function confirmed, the other being [[Mary (Lilo & Stitch)|Mary]]. Interestingly, both debuted in ''[[Stitch! The Movie]]''. *With only one brief animated scene and no other appearances in [[Lilo & Stitch (franchise)|the franchise]] (apart from his image being used in ''[[The Origin of Stitch]]'' and erroneously referred to as Experiment 144), Huggo most likely has the least amount of screen time out of all the fully confirmed experiments. (The aforementioned Mary has a briefer, less animated scene in ''Stitch! The Movie'', but she also appears animated in ''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''.) *Huggo is one of the only known experiments with six limbs; in this case, they are tentacles. [[Swapper]] also has six limbs, but only uses two or four for locomotion. *Huggo, [[Clink]], and [[Thresher]] are the only known experiments with stalked eyes, a trait common in the invertebrates that all three are inspired by. *Huggo and Thresher have very similar heads/faces. Perhaps they were created using some of the same DNA. *Huggo and [[Yin]] are the only known experiments based on cephalopods. Though given Huggo and Thresher's uncanny resemblance, Thresher may also be cephalopod-like. *Huggo's [[Experiment Pods|pod]] changes color between scenes. The Movie'', he was purple, but in ''[[The Origin of Stitch]]'', he was blue. *Huggo is one of the few experiments to not have his one true place revealed. *He is also one of the few experiments to not appear in the group photo at the end of ''Leroy & Stitch''. ==Gallery== Stitch! It is also shown that when Yin and Yang combine their powers, they are able to create rock/land. ==Appearances== ===''[[Lilo & Stitch: The Series]]''=== Experiment 501 was the 501st genetic experiment created by [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] with [[Dr. Hämsterviel|Hämsterviel]]'s funding. She was designed to spray surging water. 501 and the other first 624 experiments were deactivated and smuggled to Earth by Jumba during his mission to capture [[Stitch |Experiment 626]]. All of the experiment pods were released and scattered across the island of Kauai, with 501's pod landing in a palm tree. 501's pod fell out of the tree and into a neighbor's pool below, activating the experiment. After the woman relaxing in the pool fled in fear, 501 absorbed the pool's water and, armed, set out to cause chaos. 501 traveled to [[Lahui Beach|the beach]], where she was soon discovered by a little boy. When the boy squirted 501 with a super-soaker, the latter responded by attacking him and the rest of the beach with blasts of surging water. 501 later entered and attacked [[Kokaua Town]]. [[Stitch]] tied 501's tentacles together to render her defenseless, but this only caused her pain and her stored water to gush out and cause a flash flood. Stitch's incompetence caused a rift between him and [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]], and the two insisted that they each could catch an experiment without the other. After wagering an official contest, Stitch joined up with [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]] while Lilo joined up with [[Pleakley]], with each pair hunting down an individual experiment. 501 was later chased by Lilo and Pleakley through a jungle, but the two failed to catch the former. While draining a pond to arm herself, Experiments 501 and [[Yang|502]] met for the first time. Jumba erroneously stated that if they both touched in any way, Earth would be destroyed. However, they were ambushed and captured in [[Prison Capsule|containment orbs]] by [[Captain Gantu|Gantu]] before they could make physical contact. While returning to [[Gantu's Ship|his ship]] with the two captured experiments, Gantu fell for a sandwich trap laid by [[Reuben|Experiment 625]], allowing 501 and 502 to escape. When Stitch later tracked 501 down to a backyard, the latter used a running tap to gain an infinite supply of water to use as ammo. However, her ammo ran out when Lilo turned the tap off, allowing Stitch to easily capture 501 in a container. 501 and 502 were then rehabilitated, named Yin and Yang, and given a one true place using their combined powers to create a whole new island. Yin reappeared in "[[Elastico (episode)|Elastico]]" as one of the audience members for Lilo's hula dance. In "[[Houdini (episode)|Houdini]]", Yin was one of the audience members for Stitch's bungled magic act. In "[[Finder (episode)|Finder]]", Yin was seen playing poker with Stitch, Yang, [[Richter]], and [[Cannonball]]. In "[[Dupe (episode)|Dupe]]", Yin was one of the experiments that came to Lilo and Stitch's slumber party wearing a pink bathrobe and matching nightcap. However, she was forced by Pleakley to leave due to her destructive behavior. In "[[Angel (episode)|Angel]]", Yin was one of the experiments that [[Angel (Lilo & Stitch)|Angel]] reverted to evil using her song. Later, Yin and the other depraved experiments attacked Stitch aboard a ship, but Angel turned them to good again before they could finish Stitch off. Working together, the experiments were then able to successfully escape the ship with Stitch. Yin reappeared in "[[Slugger (episode)|Slugger]]" as part of Lilo's softball team. In "[[Shoe (episode)|Shoe]]", Yin was one of the experiments that helped turn [[Jumba's Ship|Jumba's ship]] into a [[Jumba & Pleakley's Bed & Not Breakfast|hotel]]. Yin was one of the experiments in "[[Checkers (episode)|Checkers]]" that joined Stitch in a rebellion against Gantu. Earlier in the episode, she, along with [[Digger]] and [[Backhoe]], helped Lilo make mud. In "[[Ace (episode)|Ace]]", when [[Mortlegax]] arrived on Earth to decide whether or not Jumba was still evil, Yin and Yang posed as mutant creations as part of a hoax to fool the head of E.G.O. industries. ===''[[Leroy & Stitch]]''=== In the film's opening, Yin can be seen waving hello to [[Lilo Pelekai|Lilo]], along with [[Yang]] and [[Cannonball]]. She was also seen later in the movie creating a new island with Yang as Lilo was making her rounds with [[Scrump]] to make sure all the experiments were happy in the one true place they belonged. Later, the first 624 experiments, including Yin and Yang, were rounded up by [[Leroy]] and taken to a stadium to be destroyed. However, Lilo, [[Stitch]], [[Jumba Jookiba|Jumba]], [[Pleakley]], [[Reuben]], and [[Captain Gantu|Gantu]] arrived before the experiments could be destroyed. Yin and Yang participated in the following battle between the experiments and the Leroy clones by using their combined powers to encase Leroys in rock. Yin also sprayed water at attacking Leroys until a Leroy clone completely tied her tentacles up, leaving her powerless and Yang to fight on his own. However, the Leroys soon gained the upper hand in the battle, but were defeated when Lilo, Stitch, Reuben, and several other experiments performed the song "[[Aloha ʻOe]]", which caused the Leroy army to shut down due to the original Leroy's fail-safe. ===''[[Stitch!]]''=== Yin made an appearance in the ''Stitch!'' anime special ''Stitch and the Planet of Sand''. ==Gallery== {{Gallerylink}} ==Trivia== *Yin was first revealed in a DVD bonus feature of ''[[Stitch!
